title: Trim and Lift off on a block main clip write only the group row; the members keep playing and Lift leaves the block on the clip row
scenario: In an adopted project, a main clip grouped in Full with a group effect or animated transform is a block unit, and R.isMain is true for it. The tray offers Length, Lift off and A/D. planTrimTail and planTrimHead write duration (and fxShift and keys) on the group layer only, while every following clip ripples by dt. The members still render their full spans and overlap n. planLift calls setFlag(group,'main',false), which leaves the members' sm.main alone, so the block stays main and n slides under it (an overlap chip), with its followers pinned.
why: A block is a valid main unit (§5.2), and DESIGN applies spans to every member (setUnitSpan, §3.3). Split and Duplicate already refuse blocks; trims and lift do not.
fix: Refuse trims and lift when map.get(id).type==='group' (as Split and Duplicate do), or apply the trim to every member and clear sm.main on the picture members.

verdict.evidence:
I tried to show a main block can't reach these commands, and failed. Every link in the chain holds. (I didn't re-check the 2.2 refactor after 335a3e67.)

1. A block can be a main unit. js/spine.js:122-125 (isBlockGroup) makes a group with a group effect, a non-normal blend, opacity under 1 or an animated transform into a unit, and its descendants become `members` (spine.js:145). In an adopted project, spine.js:256-262 sets `flagged = members.some(m => m.sm.main)` and puts kind 'block' into mainUnits. Members are read, not the group: setFlag refuses `main` on a group (spine.js:39), and DESIGN §2.3 (line 373) says a block's membership is its members' flags. So a sm.main clip that was grouped in Full with a group effect becomes a main block. Its R.main entry id is the group id (spine.js:353) and R.isMain(groupId) is true (spine.js:378).

2. The commands are reachable. A main tile's click selects layer.id, which here is the group (simple-timeline.js:233-235, 175). trayFor's R.isMain branch (simple-tools.js:127-133) offers Length and Lift off for it, with no block check. A/D (editor-mode.js:260-273) resolve the group through mainAtTime. S.cmd.length, trimStartBy and lift (spine-edit.js:1269, 1278-1279) and the trimTail/trimHead keys (868-869) have no guard. Split refuses because the group's type isn't in its list (spine-edit.js:567), and Duplicate refuses `L.type === 'group'` (spine-edit.js:617). The trims and Lift have no such check.

3. The trims write only the group row. In planTrimTail (spine-edit.js:477-479), `[L].concat(twins)` with L as the group sets `x.duration` on the group alone. planTrimHead (spine-edit.js:520-525) shifts duration, fx clock and keys on the group alone. Both then ripple R.main[i+1..] by dt. Members still play their own windows:
   - collectGroupUnits (compositor.js:18362) never checks the group's time span.
   - buildGroupUnit draws each member with drawLayer, gated by FM.isLayerVisibleAt(member) (scene.js:1147), and audio uses the same gate.
   - refitTransparentGroups only touches groups with no R.units entry (spine-edit.js:234), so a block row is never refit.

   Example: adopted A 0-4, B 4-8, C 8-12, all sm.main; in Full, B is grouped into G with a blur. Length on G set to 2 gives G.duration=2, B still 4-8, C moved to 6-10. Simple then shows a clean join, but B's picture and sound play over C from 6 to 8. A head trim leaves B's footage untouched while C still slides left.

4. Lift doesn't take the block off the row. planLift's post step (spine-edit.js:1099) calls `S.setFlag(L,'main',false)` with L as the group. That does nothing: groups never carry sm.main. B keeps sm.main, so the next read still finds G main. Meanwhile the ripple (dt = -(n.start - c.start)) moved C to 4-8, under G, which gives an overlap chip. G's followers are also pinned sm.stay, and FM.moveLayers (app.js:5414) moves only the group row, not its members.

5. This breaks the contract. DESIGN line 1888 says a main block with one spine member is trimmed through that member, and any other main block refuses Trim with the block line. DESIGN line 809 says membership changes on a block go through setMembership on its picture members. The code does neither.

Undo does restore all of this, so the harm is a wrong edit, not data loss. Minor is the right severity.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Smallest correct fix: refuse a main block in all three plans, as Split and Duplicate already do. This matches DESIGN line 1888 for the trims; trimming through the single spine member can come in a later release.

js/spine-edit.js
- planTrimTail, after `const c = R.main[i], ..., L = map.get(c.id), ml = MINLEN();` add:
  `if (L.type === 'group') return refusePlan('splitBlock');`
  (or a new 'blockTrim' line, "Open in Full to change this block's length", with the Open in Full button)
- planTrimHead: the same line, after L is read.
- planLift: the same line, after L is read. Making Lift work on a block properly would mean clearing sm.main on every unitLayers(c.id, map) member and moving the whole run in z, not only the group row. That is more than a minimal fix.

Optional: in simple-tools.js trayFor, hide Length and Lift off when `l.type === 'group'`, so the tray doesn't offer a tool that always refuses.

Test that fails before the fix (adopted, images or srcW/srcH set so nothing is 'undecided'):
- Set P.sm.adopted=true and build A 0-4, B 4-8, C 8-12 with sm.main on each.
- Add G {type:'group', start:4, duration:4, effects:[{type:'blur', enabled:true}]} and set B.parent=G.id.
- Assert FM.spine.read().isMain(G.id).
- `await FM.spine.cmd.length(G.id, 2)`: before the fix it returns true and leaves C.start 6 with B.start+B.duration 8 (B ends past C's start). After the fix it returns false, FM.spine.lastRefusal is the block refusal, and C.start is still 8.
- `await FM.spine.cmd.lift(G.id)`: before the fix FM.spine.read().isMain(G.id) is still true and C.start is 4. After the fix it is refused and C.start is still 8.

title: Into row leaves the clip's sound twin behind: Lift off then Into row puts the sound len seconds late
scenario: Clip c has an extracted sound twin. Lift off keeps the twin with c (unpinned), and n slides to c.start. On the next classify the twin is an audio follower of n. Into row on c picks the cut at n.start: o lands at the seam and ripple(j,+len) moves n and its followers, twin included, by +len. The picture and its own sound are now len apart.
why: §3.2 rule 7 (companions travel as one) and §4.6 (a twin belongs to its clip's unit). planIntoRow never looks for o's twins.
fix: Find twins of o among R's followers (isTwinOf(t, o)), add them to the ripple's skip set and land them with o.

verdict.evidence:
I traced the claim through the code at 335a3e67 and it holds. Into row (S.planIntoRow, js/spine-edit.js:1113-1137) never looks for the overlay's twins, and nothing later puts them back.

Concrete trace: clips A 0-3, B 3-6 and C 6-9. B has an extracted twin Bs: FM.extractAudio (js/app.js:1068-1093) makes a duplicate at 3-6 with audioOnly set, mutes B, and sets no karaokeOf and no sm.twin.

1. Lift off on B (planLift, :1084-1110). The followers fol = [Bs] are in the ripple's skip set (:1094), so Bs stays at 3. Line 1100 deliberately gives Bs no Stay put (`!S.isTwinOf(f, L, R.eps)`). C slides to 3. B and Bs are now both at 3-6, still in sync, and Lift's own test shows this half is intended ("sync twins stay with c", DESIGN §3.6 Make overlay row).
2. Next classify (js/spine.js:388-402). Nothing in the classifier links a twin to its clip; spine.js only gained two flags in this diff. Bs is an audio unit with no stay, and its host comes from the start rule: mainAt(3) = C. The sound rule does not apply (`u.end 6 > C.end 6 + 1.0` is false), and isLong is false (Bs does not start at A, and there is no clip after C). So R.followers[C] = [B, Bs]; B lands there by the same start rule.
3. Into row on B. insertIndexAt(R, 3) gives j = 1 (the cut A.end = 3, distance 0), so seam = 3 and len = 3. `ripple(plan, R, 1, 3, new Set([B.id]), 6, true)` (:1124) lands C at 6 and runs `(R.followers[e.id]||[]).forEach(f => { if (!skip.has(f)) addMove(p, f, d); })` (:296). B is skipped, but Bs gets +3. Then addLand(B, 3) (:1126).
4. couplingBlock does not stop it. An extracted twin has no karaokeOf, so refsOf(Bs) is empty. The runner (S.edit, :789-847; applyPlan, :654-673) has no twin fix-up afterwards.

Result: B (muted picture) at 3-6 and Bs (its voice) at 6-9, playing under C. The edit commits as one undo step with no warning. Before step 3, B and Bs still pass isTwinOf, so the fix can find the twin.

This breaks DESIGN §4.6: "A twin belongs to its clip's unit, like a group member: never a follower", and every command that moves c carries its twins. Lift off honours this; Into row breaks it.

The same omission shows up in other cases:
- A karaoke twin (karaokeOf = B) is refused instead, as a false 'slip' (couplingBlock :366, since dx = 3 and dy = 0).
- An overlay whose twin is in R.tail is shifted by tailMove (:1125) while the overlay lands at the seam.
- An overlay with an extracted twin made in Full has the same problem: the twin follows whichever main clip it starts on and is rippled or left behind, while the overlay lands at the seam.

The only test for Into row (tests.js diff, "Lift off makes a clip an overlay… Into row puts it back") has no twin, so it cannot catch this.

title: Delete's middle cut of a whole-video muted video drops its tail flag and says it 'keeps the length you gave it'
scenario: A first arranging Delete of a middle clip under a muted whole-video video (a light-leak texture, for example). pinStrays gives it stay + tail with tailEnd = the old end. Case (iii) splits it, and B, a clone, keeps tailEnd = the old end. B is head-trimmed to end exactly at the new trackEnd. fitTails sees |B.end − tailEnd| = len and B not in plan.resized (only l is). It clears B's tail and adds the note '…keeps the length you gave it'. The next delete leaves it running past the end.
why: The §4.3 Delete cut is meant to leave a 0..end item tail-flagged. The resized exemption covers only the original id, not the half the cut created.
fix: In the (iii) pre step, add B.id to plan.resized (or set B.sm.tailEnd to B's new end when it carries tail).

verdict.evidence:
I traced the full path and the claim holds.

1. The plan is built before anything is pinned. In S.edit (js/spine-edit.js:803), `makePlan(R)` runs first. adopt/pinStrays only run later, at :820-821. So the light leak still has no `sm.stay` when planDelete's cut filter (:397-403) is built, and the filter selects it. Why the filter selects it:
   - It is a muted video that draws a picture, so its kind is 'overlay' (js/spine.js:203).
   - It starts on clip 1 and covers the whole track, so classify makes it long with no host (js/spine.js:397-398).
   - It is not in R.tail, because it starts at 0 (:400).
   - For a middle clip c, s=0 < a and e=trackEnd > b=n.start, so it takes the media (iii) branch (:422-433). `plan.resized.add(l.id)` (:434) records only the original id.

2. pinUnits then pins it (:181-185). `whole` is true, and tailOk passes because it is a muted video of kind overlay (:146-151). It gets stay + tail + `tailEnd = e`, the OLD track end. adopt() sets the same flags if this is the first edit.

3. In applyPlan, the pre step calls FM.splitLayer. That uses FM.cloneLayer(layer, true), a full JSON deep copy (js/scene.js:828). B therefore inherits `sm = {stay, tail, tailEnd: oldEnd}`, and splitLayer never touches `sm` (js/app.js:4941ff). B is then head-trimmed by len (:429-430). It stays at start a and now ends at oldEnd − len, the new track end. `setFlag(B,'stay',true)` does not clear tail (js/spine.js:42-46).

4. fitTails (:196-224):
   - The lineage guard keeps B, the later-starting half, and clears tail on the head half.
   - For B, `fitted = oldEnd` and `e = oldEnd − len`, so |e − fitted| = len > eps.
   - `plan.resized.has(B.id)` is false, so B loses tail, keeps stay, and the line adds "… keeps the length you gave it" (:212).

5. Nothing puts the flag back:
   - pinTailsAfter (:849-856) only walks S._pinnedNow. That holds the head half's id after pinStrays, or nothing after adopt. It never holds B.
   - On the next Delete, B has sm.stay, so it is excluded from the cut (:399) and from R.tail (js/spine.js:391). It is not refit either, so it runs past the new end with the black band.

DESIGN.md §4.3 (lines 1590-1596) says this must not happen. A Delete cut is supposed to leave a 0..end item ending at the new trackEnd still carrying sm.tail, with "the tail fit then runs on it as a no-op". The doc quotes this exact "pinned with sm.stay alone … left a black band" outcome as the earlier bug. The existing test (tests/tests.js:121147-121170) only covers a whole-video TITLE, which takes the non-media (iii) branch: no split, same id, so resized exempts it. Nothing tests a muted or silent video, which takes the split branch, so the gap goes uncaught. Sound is unaffected (tailOk/setFlag refuse tail on audio), and an unmuted video with audio never gets tail. So this only affects picture videos with no audible sound, such as a light leak, grain or a muted b-roll overlay.
verdict.corrected_fix:
In planDelete's media (iii) pre step (js/spine-edit.js:424-432), right after B is found and head-trimmed, add `plan.resized.add(B.id);`. The `plan` in scope there is the same object fitTails later receives. With this line, fitTails exempts B from the "set on purpose" test. B then either already sits within 1e-9 of the new end (tailEnd = end), or it is fitted onto it and tailEnd is rewritten. An equivalent alternative is `if (B.sm && B.sm.tail) B.sm.tailEnd = (+B.start || 0) + (+B.duration || 0);` in the same place.

Test (fails before the fix, passes after):
- Set up an adopted project with main clips A(0,4), B(4,4), C(8,4) flagged sm.main.
- Add an unflagged muted full-length video overlay 'Leak' at 0..12. It has no keys and no sm, as if added in Full after adoption.
- Select B and press Backspace.
- Take the latest-starting 'Leak' half, L2 (start 4). Assert:
  - `L2.sm.tail === true` and |L2.sm.tailEnd − 8| < 1e-9 (before the fix, tail is gone);
  - `v.say()` does not match /keeps the length you gave it/ (before the fix, it does).
- Then delete C and assert L2 now ends at 4, the new track end (before the fix, it still ends at 8, past the end).
- Control: the same sequence with an image 'Leak' already passes today, because the non-media (iii) branch keeps its id in plan.resized.

title: Trims check the blend on one side only, so a crossfade can be shortened into a red overlap chip
scenario: p 0–5 and c 4–10 fade in over 4–5 (blend, amt 1). Length row: c's end typed as 1.5. planTrimTail checks only the c|n seam, so c becomes 4–5.5. blendMax(p,c)=0.75 < 1, so the seam now classifies as 'overlap' with a red Fix chip, and Close all gaps would remove the crossfade. A head trim of c with a c|n blend has the same hole (line 511).
why: DESIGN §3.1: 'No command may leave a blend seam with blendMax < amt … a trim of either clip stops at newDuration ≥ 2·amt'.
fix: In both trims, refuse (fadesBefore / fadesNext) when the new duration is under 2·amt of the blend on either side.

verdict.evidence:
The claim holds. I read both trims end to end, along with the classifier, the runner and the callers.

**Tail trim, the side it skips.** `planTrimTail` (js/spine-edit.js:457-497) checks only the seam after c (lines 465-468: `if (n && n.seam && n.seam.kind === 'blend') { if (newDur < 2 * n.seam.amt - SLACK) return refusePlan('fadesNext'); ... }`). It never reads `c.seam`, which is the seam with the clip before it. `planTrimHead` (503-548) has the mirror-image hole: lines 510-513 check only `c.seam`, never `R.main[i+1].seam`.

**Nothing downstream catches it.**
- In the runner `S.edit` (789-847), the plan is applied, then `R2 = S.classify(FM.scene)` is used only for `fitTails`, `pinTailsAfter` and `refitTransparentGroups`. Nothing compares seams or new anomalies against R.
- `ripple` (284-305) moves n by the trim amount and keeps the overlap. It does not re-check `blendMax`.
- The classifier (js/spine.js:246 `blendMax = 0.5*min(durations)`, js/spine.js:350 `else if (diff <= blendMax(prev, u) && isBlend(prev, u)) seam = blend; else overlap + anomaly`) reclassifies the seam from durations alone. That is the same in adopted mode, and a trim is gated, so adopt() runs first.

**Callers.**
- The Length row: js/simple-tools.js:169 for a typed value, and js/simple-tools.js:166 for the ± buttons.
- The A and D keys: js/editor-mode.js:273 into `S.cmd.trimHead` / `S.cmd.trimTail` (868-869).
- `S.cmd.length` / `trimStartBy` (1278-1279).

All of them go straight into these planners.

**Tail scenario confirmed.** p 0–5, c 4–10, c above with opacity keys at 4 and 5. `blendMax` = 2.5, so the seam is a blend with amt 1. Typing 1.5 in the Length row gives `newDur` 1.5. It passes MIN_LEN, and when c is the last clip n is null, so no check runs at all. The result is c at 4–5.5 with its keys still at 4 and 5, so `isBlend` stays true. But `blendMax` is now 0.75, which is less than 1, so the seam becomes 'overlap' and gets a red chip. Close all gaps (line 1172, `sm.kind === 'overlap'`) would then close it, and the crossfade is gone.

**Head scenario confirmed.** c 4–10, n 9–15 fading over c, amt 1. The start-edge Length value 1.5 gives h = 4.5. c becomes 4–5.5 and n ripples to 4.5–10.5. Overlap is still 1, `blendMax` is 0.75, so it becomes an overlap. With a larger amt it gets worse: c 4–10, n 8–14 (amt 2), trimmed to 1 s, puts n at 3, before c starts, and the main-track order flips.

**Contract.** DESIGN.md:513-514 says *"No command may leave a blend seam with `blendMax < amt` … a trim of either clip stops at `newDuration ≥ 2·amt`"*. "Either clip" means either clip of the blend, whichever edge is trimmed. The code's own Split (lines 567-568) and the Speed spec (DESIGN.md:804, "either adjacent blend") check both sides, so the trims are the odd ones out.

**No test covers it.** I found no 980 test in tests/tests.js that exercises `fadesNext`/`fadesBefore` or a blend on the far side of a trim.
verdict.corrected_fix:
In js/spine-edit.js, add the missing other-side check to each trim. Refuse rather than reclassify, using the existing lines.

planTrimTail, right after the existing n-side block (after line 468):
```js
const p = R.main[i - 1] || null;
if (p && !p.slot && c.seam && c.seam.kind === 'blend' && newDur < 2 * c.seam.amt - SLACK) return refusePlan('fadesBefore');
```

planTrimHead, right after the existing p-side block (after line 514):
```js
const n = R.main[i + 1] || null;
if (n && !n.slot && n.seam && n.seam.kind === 'blend' && d0 - h < 2 * n.seam.amt - SLACK) return refusePlan('fadesNext');
```

Extending a clip can never trip these: a blend seam already implies d0 ≥ 2·amt.

**Test (fails before the fix).** Name it '980 2.1 a trim never shortens a clip under 2x the crossfade on its OTHER side'.

1. **Fixture A.** p 0–5, then c 4–10 above it in z, with c's opacity keys at t=4 (0) and t=5 (1). c is the last clip. Assert that `FM.spine.classify(FM.scene).main[1].seam` is `{kind:'blend', amt:1}`.
   - `await FM.spine.cmd.length(c.id, 1.5)` should return false, with `FM.spine.lastRefusal === 'fadesBefore'` and `c.duration === 6`.
   - Re-classify: the seam is still 'blend' and there is no 'overlap' in `anomalies`.
   - Control: `cmd.length(c.id, 2)` passes and the seam stays a blend.
2. **Fixture B.** c 4–10, then n 9–15 above c with opacity keys at 9 and 10.
   - `await FM.spine.cmd.trimStartBy(c.id, 4.5)` should return false, with `lastRefusal === 'fadesNext'` and the document byte-identical.
   - Control: `trimStartBy(c.id, 4)` passes and the c|n seam stays a blend with amt 1.

Before the fix, both commands commit and the re-classified seam is 'overlap'.

title: Close all gaps: the hairline test misses black frames on a frame-aligned edge, and moved hairlines are never landed
scenario: (a) A clip ends exactly on frame k (k/30) and the next starts 0.012 s later. floor(prevEnd·fps)=floor(start·fps)=k, so frameIn is false and it is not fixed, yet frame k is black (prev is invisible at t=end, next is not yet visible). The opposite case, start on frame k, is 'fixed' with no frame inside. (b) A hairline after a closed gap moves by acc (off-grid) and is not landed. Whether a frame falls inside it changes (probability amt·fps).
why: A frame k is black iff prevEnd ≤ k/fps < start, which needs ceil-based tests. §3.1 says the runner lands a hairline whenever it moves, and invariant 13 forbids new black frames in the moved range (ripple() does this through isFloatJoin; planCloseAll does not).
fix: Use Math.ceil(prevEnd·fps − 1e-9) !== Math.ceil(start·fps − 1e-9), and also fix every hairline once acc ≠ 0.

verdict.evidence:
I checked both halves of the claim against the code, and both are real. Part (b) is the serious one, because Close all gaps itself creates the black frame.

**How the code behaves**
- Visibility is `t >= start && t < start + duration` (js/scene.js:1147-1148).
- Export samples frames at `start + f/fps` (js/exporter.js:1468/1477). So frame k is black exactly when `prevEnd <= k/fps < next.start`. Detecting that needs a ceil test; the floor test gets it wrong.
- A hairline is `-eps <= diff < -1e-9`, with `eps = 0.5/fps` (js/spine.js:114, :345).

**Part (a): js/spine-edit.js:1171 tests the wrong side of the hairline**
`frameIn = floor(prevEnd*fps + 1e-9) !== floor(start*fps + 1e-9)`.
- Fixture at 30 fps: A [0,2), C [2.012, 4.012), with a 0.5 s gap later so the ⋯ entry is offered (simple-tools.js:195 shows it only when there is a gap or overlap).
- floor(60) = floor(60.36) = 60, so frameIn is false.
- acc is 0 when C is reached, so C is neither landed nor moved.
- Frame 60 (t = 2.0) is black before and after the command: A ends at exactly 2, C starts at 2.012.
- DESIGN.md §3.6 table (line 813) and §13 #55 say Close all gaps closes a hairline whenever a frame time falls inside it. This one has a frame inside and stays open.
- The opposite case (prevEnd off-grid, start exactly on a frame) is "fixed" and counted in `closed` with no frame inside. That over-closes, which is harmless, but it inflates the count.

**Part (b): a hairline after a closed gap moves off-grid and is never landed**
- In planCloseAll (1168-1177), a hairline with `fix` false gets `addMove(e.id, acc)`. Nothing re-lands it.
- applyPlan (654-672) and the runner (S.edit, 815-826) have no landing pass after the plan is applied.
- Every other command does land a moved hairline:
  - `ripple()` lands any hairline it moves, through `isFloatJoin` (118, 291).
  - Close gap goes through `ripple`.
  - Move clip (Reorder) lands moved hairlines explicitly (1054).
- §3.1 says a hairline is "landed shut whenever it moves". Invariant 13 (DESIGN.md:1241) excludes only "a hairline that did not move and was not created by the command".

I worked it through in Python with IEEE doubles. Fixture at 30 fps: A [0,2), B [2.52, 4.51), C [4.522, 6.522).
1. B's seam is a gap (0.52 s). C's seam is a hairline (0.012 s): floor(135.3) = floor(135.66), so frameIn is false.
2. Before the command, no frame falls inside the hairline.
3. Close all lands B at 2, so acc = -0.52, and C moves to 4.002.
4. B now ends at 3.99. Frame 120 (t = 4.0) is in neither clip: **a new black frame in the export, created by the command.**

**Why the suite misses it**
T2 (the seeded-invariants test in tests/tests.js) runs del, trimTail, trimHead, split, closeSeam and dup, but never closeAll. The only closeAll test (the "Simple's ⋯ offers Close all gaps" test, tests.js diff line 761) checks the menu and the step count, not frames.
verdict.corrected_fix:
In S.planCloseAll (js/spine-edit.js:1168-1173), change two things:
1. Use a ceil-based frame test, measured on the original positions.
2. Also land every hairline that the command moves (acc !== 0). Count only real closures in `closed`.

```js
const pEnd0 = k ? R.main[k - 1].end : 0;
const hair = sm && sm.kind === 'hairline';
const frameIn = hair && Math.ceil(pEnd0 * fps0 - 1e-9) !== Math.ceil(e.start * fps0 - 1e-9);
const movedHair = hair && acc !== 0 && prevEnd != null;          // §3.1: landed shut whenever it moves
const fix = sm && !sm.covered && (sm.kind === 'gap' || sm.kind === 'overlap' || frameIn || movedHair || (sm.kind === 'join' && Math.abs(pEnd0 - e.start) < 1e-9 && prevEnd != null));
if (fix) { const target = prevEnd != null ? prevEnd : 0; if (sm.kind === 'gap' || sm.kind === 'overlap' || frameIn) closed++; acc += target - ns; d = acc; ns = target; }
```

The landing goes through addLand as before. Later clips, their followers and the tail take the correction through acc, the same way ripple() does.

**Tests that fail before the fix**, at 30 fps, plain main clips, no background, run through FM.spine.cmd.closeAll():

(i) A [0,2), B [2.52, 4.51), C [4.522, 6.522):
- Expect `C.start === B.start + B.duration` bit for bit.
- Expect smBlackFrames(FM.spine.classify(FM.scene)) to be empty.
- Today C.start is 4.002 and frame 4.0 s is black.

title: Append moves an end card but never refuses (or maps) a keyed camera, so a zoom on the card now plays over the new clips
scenario: Clips 0–10, a logo card 10–13, camera keys 10–13 zooming on the logo. Append a 5 s clip: R.tail moves +5 to 15–18, but the camera keys stay at 10–13, so the zoom plays over the new clip and the card is unzoomed. Every other 2.1/2.2 command catches this through riderBlock's camera check.
why: DESIGN §3.10 rule 3e: the camera goes through the Append map whenever the plan moves the tail. 2.1/2.2 refuse instead of half-applying (§3.2 rule 6), but planAppend only checks R.riders.
fix: When R.tail is non-empty, run riderBlock(R, T, map) in planAppend and refuse on a camera result.

verdict.evidence:
I traced the path end to end in the worktree at 335a3e67 and could not refute the claim.

1. **The end card is in R.tail, and the camera is in R.fullOnly.**
   - js/spine.js:192 puts a `type === 'camera'` layer in fullOnly, which is pushed to R.fullOnly at :387.
   - The card at 10–13 has no stay flag, starts at or after trackEnd and has no main clip under it, so js/spine.js:400 pushes it to R.tail.
   - Neither adopt nor pinStrays pins it: S.neverPinned returns true for R.tail (spine-edit.js:140), and pinUnits skips neverPinned units.

2. **S.planAppend (js/spine-edit.js:965-995) moves the card and leaves the camera alone.**
   - It refuses only riders that cross T (line 969).
   - It then calls `R.tail.forEach(id => addMove(plan, id, sum))` (line 980).
   - It never calls riderBlock, and there is no other camera check in the function.

3. **Nothing later in the edit maps or refuses the camera.**
   - The runner S.edit (789-850) does: refusal → gate → locks → adopt/pinStrays → applyPlan → fitTails/refitTransparentGroups → commit.
   - applyPlan (654-670) shifts keys only for ids in plan.moves or plan.lands. The camera is in neither, and unitLayers never reaches it.
   - fitTails skips cameras (tailOk returns false for a camera).
   - FM.autoFitDuration only stretches a start-0 camera's window. It never moves keys.

4. **Result for the scenario** (clips 0–10, card 10–13, camera scale keys 10–13, Append a 5 s clip):
   - The card goes to 15–18 and the camera keys stay at 10–13.
   - So the zoom plays over the new clip and the card plays unzoomed.
   - This is one committed undo step with no warning.

5. **This breaks both specs.**
   - It contradicts DESIGN §3.10 rule 3e: the camera goes through the Append map whenever the plan moves the tail.
   - It contradicts BUILD-PLAN-PHASE2's own 2.1/2.2 policy. The plan lists "the camera's keys or window after it" as a refusal, and §13 says that until 2.4 "a keyed camera … refuses the arranging commands that would touch it".
   - An Append that moves the tail is arranging: `plan.arranges = R.tail.length > 0`.
   - §14.5 lists Append's accepted deviations (cues past the end not shifted; a straddling caption track refused). The camera is not among them.
   - Every other 2.1/2.2 command that moves things calls riderBlock, including Insert at 1004, which uses its camera half. Append is the only gap.

6. **No test covers it.** No Phase 2 test in tests/tests.js mentions a camera.

Severity minor is right: the result is a wrong edit that can be undone, with no data loss.

title: Insert / Into row after a slot pass the slot entry's id to moveLayers, so the new clips drop to the bottom of the stack
scenario: A card (slot) between Clip 2 and Clip 3, with the playhead near the card's end. insertIndexAt picks j = slot index + 1, so before = R.main[j−1] is {id:'slot:…'}. FM.moveLayers(made, 'slot:…') finds no such layer and appends the clips at the end of the array, under any background or behind layer, where they can be hidden. The Clips tool's label for that cut also reads 'After ' with no name. planIntoRow line 1130 has the same issue.
why: R.main contains slot entries, whose ids are not layer ids.
fix: Walk back to the nearest non-slot entry (or use the slot's first member) for the z anchor, and in the label say 'After the card'.

verdict.evidence:
The claim holds. I traced it end to end in the 980-phase2 worktree.

1. Card entries in R.main have ids that are not layer ids. js/spine.js:338 and :348 push `{ id: 'slot:' + mem[0].id, slot: true, ... }` into `main`. No layer id ever starts with 'slot:'.

2. Insert can land straight after a card.
   - `S.insertIndexAt` (spine-edit.js:915-924) loops over every R.main entry, cards included, so the cut at a card's end is a candidate.
   - `clipsTool` (simple-tools.js:89-98) passes that j on unchanged.
   - `planInsert` (spine-edit.js:1009) then sets `before = j > 0 ? R.main[j - 1] : null`, and at :1014 calls `FM.moveLayers(made.map(l => l.id), before ? before.id : e.id)`.

3. `moveLayers` sends an unknown anchor to the bottom of the stack. In js/app.js:5414-5436, `at = rest.length`, and `rest.findIndex(l => l.id === 'slot:…')` returns -1, so `at` never changes. The new clips go to the end of FM.scene.layers, which is the bottom; index 0 is the top, as the spine-edit.js:3202 comment and the existing Append z-test confirm. Nothing restacks them afterwards. `applyPlan` (:654-672) and `S.edit` (:819-826) run only fitTails, pinTailsAfter and refitTransparentGroups, and DESIGN says fitTails never changes z.

4. `planIntoRow` has the same bug at :1129-1130: `FM.moveLayers([o.id], before.id)` with a card as `before` drops the overlay to the very bottom.

5. The label is wrong too. `S.itemWord(FM.layerById(FM.scene, 'slot:…'), R)` gets null, and spine.js:78 returns '' for null, so the button reads "After ".

**It is reachable, and more easily than the claim says.** A leading title card (text at 0-2, clip A at 2-5) makes R.main[0] a card. With the playhead anywhere in the first half of Clip 1, `inside` is true and the nearest cut is j=1, so `before` is the card.

**Concrete failure.** A 9:16 project. Top to bottom: text 'Intro' 0-2, video A 2-5, video B 5-8, and a full-frame still 'Bg' 0-8 at the bottom as a letterbox backdrop.
- Clips > "After " > pick a PNG.
- The PNG lands at 2-2+d, but at layers.length-1, under Bg.
- Bg is full-frame and opaque, so nothing of the new clip shows in preview or export.
- Bg's side also flips from 'behind' to 'mixed', so it jumps out of the Behind lane.

DESIGN §3.6.1(c) names exactly this outcome as the thing to avoid: a new clip put "under a letterbox background or a template's full-canvas backdrop rect, where nothing of it showed". It also says a new main clip goes "directly above the main clip before it in main order". A card is not a main clip.

**Why tests miss it.** BUILD-PLAN-PHASE2.md:3340 has the same line, so the code follows the plan. The only Insert tests (tests.js:121593, :121668) use fixtures with no card.

Append is not affected: at :980 it already filters out cards with `R.main.filter(e => !e.slot)`.

title: Reorder decides whether to land a hairline from the entry's OLD leading seam, so the p|n hairline that c's removal creates is moved and left open
scenario: p|c is a 0.01 s hairline and c|n is an exact join. Move c later: n's new predecessor is p, gap = c.start−p.end (the hairline), but the test reads n.seam (c|n, a join), so n moves by −len and is not landed. The hairline lands at a new off-grid position, where a frame falls inside with probability amt·fps.
why: §3.1 (a): a hairline in the moved range, including one that becomes adjacent across a moved clip, is landed shut.
fix: Test the gap itself (0 < gap ≤ R.eps) instead of e.seam.kind==='hairline' when the predecessor changed.

verdict.evidence:
The bug is real, but it shows up on Move EARLIER. The claim's own example, Move LATER, does not produce the harm it describes.

The code: js/spine-edit.js:1054 decides whether to land a hairline by reading `e.seam.kind === 'hairline'`. That is the entry's OLD leading seam. After the move, the entry right after c (k === i+1, which is n) has p in front of it, not c. The gap it actually has at p|n is p|c's old amount, because L = n.start − c.start (:1036, :1045). So when p|c is a hairline and c|n is an exact join, line 1054 reads c|n ('join'). The fallback at :1055 only fires when order[pos−1] === i, and here the previous entry is p, not c. So n is not landed and the p|n hairline stays open. Delete handles the same seam correctly: :437-439 uses landFirst = isFloatJoin(R, i), which is c's own seam p|c (:118). §3.1(a) and BUILD-PLAN-PHASE2 §172 both say every hairline in the moved range is landed, including one that becomes adjacent across a removed clip. Nothing after the plan is applied (:655-673) closes it. No test covers it: the P2.2 reorder test (tests.js:121522) uses whole-second seams only.

Correction to the claim's scenario: on Move LATER, p does not move (dOf = 0 and acc = 0 before it) and n lands at n.start − L ≈ c.start. The hairline stays exactly at [p.end, c.start], so no new black frame appears. That direction only differs from what Delete does.

Where it does cause a new black frame: Move EARLIER. p is in [j, i), so it moves by +L, and n does not move. The hairline therefore moves by L to [n.start − h, n.start]. I replicated the walk at :1046-1066 in Python. Setup: fps 30 (eps 1/60), clips A[0,2) B[2,4.02) C[4.03,15.24) (11.21 s) D[15.24,18.24). Before, no frame time is uncovered. Select C and press Move earlier (j = i−1, as moveIndexFor gives): result is A[0,2) C[2,13.21) B[13.21,15.23) D[15.24,18.24). Frame 457/30 = 15.2333 is inside the hairline, so the export shows a black frame the command created. The chance of this is h·fps, up to 50%. With the fix the same walk leaves no uncovered frame.

Side note, not part of this claim: the same test at :1054 also lands hairlines LEFT of the edit point. Those have dOf = 0 and their own seam is a hairline, which goes against §3.1's 'left alone'. planReorder also has no tailMove, so any landing correction in acc is not passed on to the tail.
verdict.corrected_fix:
In S.planReorder (js/spine-edit.js ~1052-1054), choose which seam to test the way Delete does. For the entry that closes up behind c, read c's own leading seam p|c:

  const sk = (k === i + 1 && i > 0) ? R.main[i].seam : e.seam;   // across the removed c the seam is p|c's (Delete: isFloatJoin(R, i))
  if (gap != null && ((Math.abs(gap) < 1e-9 && gap !== 0) || (gap > 0 && gap <= R.eps && sk && sk.kind === 'hairline'))) { acc += prevEnd - prop; ns = prevEnd; }

Testing `gap > 0 && gap <= R.eps` when k === i + 1 is equivalent, because that gap is exactly p|c's amount.

Test that fails before the fix: 'simple P2.2 · Move earlier lands the hairline that closes up behind the moved clip'.
- Setup: smP2 at 30 fps with smV('D', 15.24, 3), smV('C', 4.03, 11.21), smV('B', 2, 2.02), smV('A', 0, 2).
- Action: select C, smTool('earlier').click(), await v.idle().
- Assert the order is A C B D and that v.L('D').start === v.L('B').start + v.L('B').duration (bit-exact).
- Assert no frame time f/30 falls in [B.end, D.start).
- Assert one undo restores v.doc().
- Before the fix, D.start is 15.24 and B ends at 15.23, so frame 457/30 = 15.2333 is uncovered.

Use Move earlier, not Move later. In the Move later version the hairline does not move, so its only check would be the bit-exact join.

title: Stay put on 2+ items is one undo step per item, and items after the fifth are silently dropped
scenario: Select 7 non-main items and tap Stay put: ids.forEach(id => S.cmd.stay(id,true)). The first runs, the next four queue, and the sixth and seventh hit the queue cap and say 'One moment — still finishing the last edit.' Only 5 items are pinned, and the change takes 5 undo presses to reverse.
why: §3.2 rule 2 (one action = one undo step), and §8.5b's tray offers Stay put (all) as one action.
fix: Add a planStayMany(R, ids, on) that writes every flag in one plan through one S.edit.

verdict.evidence:
I followed the whole path and could not refute it.

1. **The tap.** js/simple-tools.js:227 (the 2+ branch of sync) runs `ids.forEach(id => S.cmd.stay(id, true))`. js/spine-edit.js:1271 defines `stay(id,on)` as one `S.edit('Stay put', R => S.planStay(R,id,on))` per id. So a 7-item selection makes seven separate S.edit calls, all from the same click.

2. **The first call holds the runner.** S.edit (spine-edit.js:787) sets `S.running = true` straight away. For a stay plan nothing returns early: planStay (1139-1146) sets `arranges=false` and `adopts=false`, so the gates are skipped, and `touched` is empty, so there is no lock or lease refusal. It then reaches `await applyPlan(plan)` (:817). applyPlan is async, so even with `plan.pre` empty the await gives control back before S.running is cleared, and the forEach carries on.

3. **Calls 2 to 5 queue, 6 and 7 are thrown away.** Calls 2 to 5 hit `if (S.running) { if (S.queue.length < 4) S.queue.push(...) else S.say(line('wait')); return false; }` (:789-793). The queue fills to 4. Calls 6 and 7 find it full and only say 'One moment — still finishing the last edit.' (spine-words.js:50). Their intent is never stored. The drain at :778-786 later runs the four queued edits one at a time. So only 5 of the 7 items get `sm.stay`, and the user is never told that two were skipped. Each queued edit's own live line ('Stays put') then replaces the wait line.

4. **Five undo steps.** Every S.edit ends in its own `FM.history.commit({label:'Stay put', ed:'s', arr:false})` (:832). history.commit (history.js:289-323) never merges commits. Each push stores a different snapshot (a different flag changed), so there are 5 stack entries and 5 collab transactions. One ⌘Z only un-pins the fifth item.

5. **Reachable.** A 2+ selection survives the switch into Simple: editor-mode.js apply() (:123-153) never clears selectedIds, and DESIGN keeps the selection across the switch (§8.5b, line ~2100). It also arrives from paste (app.js:4496 `selectedIds = made`) and from undo (history.js:157). The tray shows Stay put whenever every selected id is non-main (`all`). With 2 to 5 items, the undo-step half of the bug still happens.

6. **The contract.** DESIGN §3.2 rule 2: "One action = one undo step = one collab transaction". §8.5b lists "Stay put (all)" as a single tray action. It writes "(each, one commit)" only for Volume and Look. The BUILD-PLAN copies the same forEach (BUILD-PLAN-PHASE2.md:2770), so the plan's code breaks its own contract. The known-gaps table (:4181) defers only the multi-Delete, not this. No test covers Stay put on several items.

A side note, not part of the claim: the runner then shrinks the selection to `[sel0]` (:829), so after the first edit the tray drops back to one item's tools.

title: A clip added or duplicated in Simple can come back blank: {noSave} drops the immediate media save and nothing replaces it
scenario: On a phone in Simple, tap Duplicate on a clip, or Clips > At the end / After Clip N, Overlay or Music. The runner's duplicateLayer / addMediaLayer calls skip their own FM.storage.save() (app.js:4449 and :3130, {noSave}). The runner then only calls FM.history.commit(...), which runs FM.storage.autosave(), a 600 ms debounce (storage.js:869). Within those 600 ms he swipes home or locks the phone. The visibilitychange handler calls flushSync (storage.js:814, :3860). flushSync writes the scene JSON, which already lists the new layer, and runs clearTimeout(saveTimer), so the pending save() is cancelled. save() is the only code that writes a layer's media blob to IndexedDB (storage.js:771). If iOS then kills the backgrounded tab, or he closes the app before making any further edit, the project reopens with the copied or added clip blank. _hydrateSceneMedia reads the record by layer.id only and has no fallback, and the Media-library tile points at the same missing key.
why: This is the exact failure queue 681 documents at app.js:5120-5128: the flush writes the document but not the footage, and the clip comes back empty. Every Full path that makes a media record under a new id saves at once for that reason. The plan says the runner's one commit saves, but commit() only schedules a save, and flushSync cancels it.
fix: In S.edit, after the successful FM.history.commit(...), call FM.storage.save() directly when the plan made media. Set a flag such as plan.minted in addRecs and in planDuplicate's pre step, or simply save whenever plan.pre ran. This writes the finished, rippled document and its blobs straight away, and still keeps the un-rippled document off disk during the run.

verdict.evidence:
I traced every path end to end in the 980-phase2 worktree and could not refute the claim.

1. Simple turns off the immediate save. planDuplicate does it at js/spine-edit.js:625 and :631 (`FM.duplicateLayer(..., { noSave: true })`). addRecs does it at :953 (`FM.addMediaLayer(it.rec, {..., noSave: true})`), and addRecs is used by planAppend (:983, :986), planInsert (:1012, :1018), planAddOverlay (:1239) and planAddMusic (:1257). That noSave flag stops the direct `FM.storage.save()` at js/app.js:3130 and :4449. The `FM.history.commit()` calls inside those functions do nothing while the runner has history muted (history.js `if (muteDepth > 0) return;` comes before the autosave), so nothing gets scheduled during the run.

2. After the run, the only save is debounced. S.edit (spine-edit.js:837) calls `FM.history.commit({label, ed:'s', arr})`. That reaches `FM.storage.autosave()` (history.js:324), which only does `clearTimeout(saveTimer); saveTimer = setTimeout(save, 600)` (storage.js:869). Nothing in spine-edit.js or simple-tools.js calls save() directly. Grepping 'storage' finds only the autosave in restorePreEdit (:686). DESIGN.md:1045-1048 says "The runner's one commit autosaves the finished result", so the designers saw it as a debounce. They did not see the hide-flush problem.

3. A hide flush cancels the pending save. The handlers at storage.js:3859-3860 (pagehide, and visibilitychange to hidden) call flushSync (:814): `clearTimeout(saveTimer); return writeScene();`. writeScene writes only the localStorage document, which already lists the new layer. save() is the only code that runs planBlobWrites, notePending and idbPut (storage.js:736-797). Nothing re-arms the save when the tab becomes visible again. _dirty only stamps the modified time.

4. The reload comes back blank and says nothing. _hydrateSceneMedia (storage.js:450+) reads `idbGetMedia(db, layer.id)` and has no fallback, so the layer lands in `lacking`. notePending never ran, so reportPending has no note and does not even show the "never finished saving" toast. mediaLib.add (medialib.js:77) still runs under noSave and only indexes `key: layer.id`. It writes no blob, so the Library tile points at the same missing record.

Concrete failure: on a phone in Simple, he taps Duplicate on Clip 2 (or Clips > At the end with a picked video). S.edit resolves and commit arms the 600 ms timer. About 300 ms later he locks the phone or swipes home. visibilitychange to hidden runs flushSync, which clears the timer and writes a document that lists the copy's layer id. iOS later kills the backgrounded PWA, or he comes back, watches, and swipes the app away (pagehide does flushSync again, still with no blobs). On reopen, the copy or the newly added clip is blank, with no message.

Full saves immediately on exactly this kind of path because of this failure: queue 681, js/app.js:5120-5128 ("pagehide/visibilitychange CANCEL the pending save and write the scene document only"). The noSave flag removes that protection on every Simple route that creates a media record. Two things limit the harm, which is why I call it narrow but real data loss. The window is only the 600 ms debounce, and any later edit heals it, because planBlobWrites writes every missing blob. No test covers it: `grep noSave tests/*.js` finds nothing.
verdict.corrected_fix:
In js/spine-edit.js S.edit, start the blob save straight after the runner's one commit, whenever the plan created media. The save then writes the finished, rippled document, so the reason for noSave still holds and nothing un-rippled reaches disk mid-run:

```js
      FM.history.commit({ label: label, ed: 's', arr: gated });
      if (plan.mints && FM.storage && FM.storage.save) FM.storage.save();   // a new media record: write its file now, not on the 600 ms debounce a hide flush cancels (queue 681)
```

Set the flag where media is created:
- planDuplicate's pre, after `dup` is confirmed: `plan.mints = true;`
- addRecs: return `made` as now, and in each pre that calls it (planAppend, planInsert, planAddOverlay, planAddMusic) set `if (made.length || (snd && snd.length)) plan.mints = true;`
- likewise for any future `swapInMedia(..., {noSave})` Replace route.

A simpler version that is also safe is `if (plan.pre.length) FM.storage.save();`. Split's pre already saves inside splitLayer, and a second save is a no-op for blobs whose stored rev matches and for an unchanged document. The 600 ms autosave still fires afterwards and is harmless.

Test, which fails before the fix (tests/tests.js, `{ item: '980' }`): open a project in Simple with one fixture video clip L. `await FM.spine.cmd.duplicate(L.id)`. Take `dupId = FM.scene.selectedId`. Then immediately call `FM.storage.flushSync()` to simulate the hidden visibilitychange, `await FM.storage.settled()`, and assert `(await FM.storage.readMedia(dupId))` has a `.file`. Before the fix, flushSync clears the only pending save, settled() resolves at once and readMedia returns null. After the fix, the save started by S.edit is in `_saving`, settled() waits for it and the record is there. Repeat with `FM.spine.edit('Add clip', R => FM.spine.planAppend(R, { clips: [{ rec: fixtureRec, len: 2 }], sounds: [] }))` for the addRecs path. Also assert `FM.storage.pendingSaves() > 0` right after the edit resolves.

title: Add clips, Insert, Overlay and Music can apply a Simple ripple after the editor has switched to Full
scenario: In Simple, he taps Clips > After Clip 2 and picks 4 videos. cmd.insert awaits S.readPicked(files) before calling S.edit; that reads each file's metadata through FM.loadVideoFile, which can take a second or more per file. During that wait S.running is false and body.sm-running is not set, so editor-mode's busyReason() (editor-mode.js:81) allows the switch. He opens the cog and switches to Full. readPicked then resolves and S.edit runs with Full on screen, because S.edit has no check that Simple is on screen. planInsert ripples every main clip after cut 2 and its followers to the right, moves end cards, and on an unadopted project runs S.adopt (sets P.sm.adopted, sm.main and Stay put flags). It moves the playhead and changes the selection, then commits a step tagged arr, which the undo door can later refuse in Full. Any refusal (locked, couplings, riders) goes to the hidden #sm-say, so in Full nothing visible happens. The same applies to cmd.append, addOverlay and addMusic.
why: Full never ripples, and Ezra's rule is that Full does not change. Here a Simple ripple, its adoption writes and its silent refusals happen in Full with no warning. The runner was meant to be unreachable from Full, but the readPicked step outside it leaves a window open.
fix: At the top of S.edit (and in drain for queued edits), refuse or drop the command when !(FM.editor && FM.editor.isSimple && FM.editor.isSimple()). Alternatively, hold a busy flag across readPicked that busyReason() reads, so the switch is refused until the add has run.

verdict.evidence:
The race is real, and nothing closes it.

1. Every file command reads its files before the runner. js/spine-edit.js:1266-1267 and :1276-1277 are `(async () => { const picked = await S.readPicked(files); return S.edit(...) })()`. readPicked (:934-948) awaits FM.loadVideoFile or FM.loadImageFile once per file, one after another. loadVideoFile (js/media.js:125-196) waits for loadedmetadata. An audio track waits for a full decode first, and a file that never answers waits up to 20 s (metaTimer). loadImageFile decodes every frame of a GIF. During all of this S.running is false, nothing has set body.sm-running (that only happens inside S.edit at :796), and no job is open.

2. The switch cannot see that wait. busyReason() (js/editor-mode.js:79-85) checks only FM._exporting, the voice recorder, `FM.spine.running || body.sm-running`, and a live drag. request() and apply() both go through it. The cog's switch therefore succeeds while readPicked is pending, and so does the 'Open in Full' hop from a Simple line.

3. S.edit (:789-848) never checks which editor is on screen. When readPicked resolves with Full showing, the whole Simple plan runs: planInsert's ripple, S.adopt on a project not yet adopted, pinStrays, fitTails, `FM.time = plan.time`, a new selection, and `history.commit({arr: gated})`.

4. Every line it speaks goes through S.say into sayLine (js/simple-timeline.js:107). That writes into #sm-say inside #sm-bar, and styles.css:11784 sets `#sm-bar { display: none; }` outside body.ed-simple. Any refusal is invisible in Full: insertFade at a crossfade cut, riders, locked with its 'Do it anyway' retry, waiting, or live/offline when a friend who can edit is in. He picked 4 videos and nothing happens, with no word. The success line is also hidden while the track ripples underneath him.

5. The plan meant to forbid this. DESIGN §3.7 says that while a Simple command is in flight "the cog's switch refuses with 'One moment…'". T8 Round 3 says "the switch refuses while a Simple command runs (sm-running)". The T2 runner case has "a cog switch tap during the await … the switch refuses". readPicked was moved before the runner only so that a picker or decode never sits inside an undo step (BUILD-PLAN-PHASE2 :2538), not to open a window for the switch. The plan did consider this exact window for a project switch: readPicked checks FM.stillIn. It did not consider the editor switch.

Where I push back: when the add succeeds, the ripple is the edit he asked for in Simple. Undoing it in Full goes through the same arr door as any Simple step, and no data is lost. So this is minor. The concrete wrong results are:
- a Simple command spoken into a hidden sink (a refused add vanishes silently in Full);
- a Simple ripple, an adoption write and a playhead jump landing after Full is already on screen, which the busy-state guard was written to prevent.

A smaller, related window: S.drain re-arms with setTimeout while jobDepth() > 0 (:782). Queued Simple edits then wait with S.running false, so a switch in that gap runs them in Full too.

The reviewer's first fix makes things worse. Refusing at the top of S.edit when !isSimple() turns every case into a silent drop, because refuse() also speaks to the hidden #sm-say. The refusal belongs on the switch, as the design says.

title: Insert lands the next clip on the new clips' end, but its followers, later clips and the tail still move by the plain sum

I could not refute it. I read the whole path from the + button to the commit, and nothing on it places the new clips in the stack when the main track is empty.

title: Deleting a clip that owns a fade-in cuts long items by b−a while the clips close up by b−a+amt, so a narration falls out of step
scenario: p 0–5. c 4–10 sits above p and fades in over 4–5 (a blend, amt 1, owned by c). n 10–15. A long voice-over N runs 2–14. Delete c: dt = p.end − n.start = −5, so n lands at 5. But len = b−a = 6, so N's split B half is head-trimmed by 6 and kept at a=4. N's audio from 10 s now plays at 4 while n's first frame is at 5: the voice runs 1 s ahead for the rest of the video. A non-media pastNext item cut by duration−len ends 1 s past the clip it ended on.
why: DESIGN's Delete row uses len = −dt for every cut unit (f(b) = b−len = p.end). The code changes dt for the owned fade but keeps len = b−a, and (i) lands at a, not at f.
fix: When plan.counts.fade is set, use len = −dt for the cut. Land case (i) and case (iii)'s B at a + (dt + (b−a)) (= p.end), or refuse cut items in this case until 2.4.

verdict.evidence:
I traced the scenario through the code and it happens as the claim says. The claim's suggested fix is wrong for case (iii), though.

The scenario is reachable:
- p (A) runs 0–5, c (B) runs 4–10 and sits above p, with opacity keys at 4 and 5. js/spine.js:350 classifies the seam as a blend: the overlap is 1, and blendMax is 0.5·min(5,6) = 2.5.
- The suite already builds this exact fixture and confirms it is a blend (tests/tests.js:121654-121660, "CONTROL: the fixture is not a crossfade").
- blendOwner (js/spine-edit.js:133) returns c, since c's index in FM.scene.layers is lower (nearer the top).
- So planDelete does not refuse. At js/spine-edit.js:387 it sets dt = p.end − n.start = −5 and counts.fade = 1.
- The ripple then lands n at exactly p.end = 5 (landFirst at :438; the landing branch inside ripple()).

The voice-over is cut through the wrong span:
- N is a voice-over at 2–14. mainAt(2) is p, and soundRuns is true because 14 > 5+1 (spine.js:397-399). So N is long and has no host.
- On the first arranging edit the plan is built from R before adopt() or pinStrays() add sm.stay (runner :805-821). So the cut filter at :396-402 picks N up.
- The span is still [a, b) = [4, 10), because :395 sets len = b − a = 6. It never uses −dt = 5.
- N falls into case (iii), media. The pre step (:423-431) splits N at FM.time = a = 4, then head-trims B by len = 6. That gives B trimStart 2+6 = 8 and duration 4.
- B's start is never written (the trimClipEdge start is ignored), and no move or landing touches B, because B is a new layer. applyPlan (:654-672) confirms nothing else changes it.

The result:
- B plays source 8–12 over 4–8, while n's first frame is now at 5.
- Before the delete, source 8 lined up with n's first frame at 10. So the voice now runs 1 s ahead for the rest of the video.
- Case (i) has the same error: an item starting inside c is head-trimmed by b − s, so its frame at b now plays at a = 4 instead of 5 (:409).
- A non-media case-(iii) item is shortened by 6 instead of 5 (:420). One small correction to the claim: that item ends 1 s before the clip it ended with, not "past" it. The tail fit repairs this only when the item ends the whole track.

The code is not following its plan correctly here. DESIGN.md:799 says a cut "goes through the command's own delete map f … len = −dt" and that case (i) footage "stays in step". It also says that when c owns the fade, n lands at p.end with dt = −(n.start − p.end).

BUILD-PLAN-PHASE2.md:570-640 copies the same `len = b - a` code, so the plan carries the same error. No test covers a fade-owned Delete with a cut item: tests/tests.js:121150 uses plain joins only.

The claim's fix does not work for case (iii). It splits at a = 4 and trims B by len = 5, then lands B at 5. That puts source 7 at time 5, so the voice is off by 1 s the other way and a silent 4–5 hole opens. The time that actually disappears is [p.end, n.start), because p still shows over [c.start, p.end). So the cut should start at p.end.
verdict.corrected_fix:
In js/spine-edit.js planDelete, after the blend block (:384-389), add a separate start for the cut. Use it everywhere in the cut section (:395-436). Leave riderBlock(R, a) as it is (it is the stricter check).

  const ca = (plan.counts.fade && n) ? p.end : a;   // c's fade-in went with it: what played at b now plays at p.end
  const ml = MINLEN(), len = b - ca;                // = -dt

Then make these replacements:
- In the cut filter: `e > a + 1e-9` becomes `e > ca + 1e-9`.
- Case (i): the test `s >= a - 1e-9` becomes `s >= ca - 1e-9`, and `addLand(plan, l.id, a)` becomes `addLand(plan, l.id, ca)`. The head-trim by b − s stays as it is.
- Case (ii): `a - s` becomes `ca - s`, both in the cutShort check and in the duration write.
- Case (iii), media: `a - s < ml` becomes `ca - s < ml`, `FM.time = a` becomes `FM.time = ca`, and the B lookup `Math.abs((+x.start||0) - a)` becomes `- ca`. Keep the head-trim by len, which is now b − ca.
- Case (iii), non-media: no edit needed; it already uses len.

With no blend, ca = a and len = b − a, so the delete behaves exactly as it does now.

title: A long video or sound with a speed ramp is cut by Delete with its ramp keys left at their old times
scenario: A long voice-over or overlay video with only a speed ramp (no other keys) overlaps the deleted span. keyCount skips layer.speed, so cutKeys does not refuse. Case (i) lands it at a with plan.keyless, so no key moves, although its footage moved by a−b. Case (iii)'s B is head-trimmed in place, and its ramp keys after b stay put. The ramp now plays (b−a) late against its footage, and the source advance (and so the sync) changes.
why: keyless exists because the keys are supposed to go through riderKeys. 2.1 instead refuses any cut item with keys, but the count leaves out the ramp, which is absolute-time keyframes like the others.
fix: Count speed keys in the cutKeys refusal (or a separate keyCount for cut items), or shift the speed list by the same d / f.

verdict.evidence:
I could not refute it. I traced the code end to end (worktree 980-phase2, read only, nothing run).

1. **The ramp is not counted.** `S.keyCount` skips `layer.speed` (js/spine-edit.js:36-39). It has one caller, the cutKeys refusal at js/spine-edit.js:405. So a long cut item whose only keys are a speed ramp gets through the refusal.

2. **The item is reachable.**
   - A sound is long when it is audio, not a twin, and ends more than 1 s past its host (js/spine.js:397-398). An overlay video is long through `isLong`.
   - Nothing in classification keeps a ramped video or sound out of the cut set; only camera/null/group/etc. are excluded (js/spine.js:189-205).
   - The runner builds the plan from R before `S.adopt` / `S.pinStrays` add `sm.stay` (js/spine-edit.js:799-821). So the first arranging Delete over a not-yet-pinned long item reaches the cut code.
   - `riderBlock` only looks at captions and the camera. `couplingBlock` only looks at references. `S.blockers` only looks at collab holds. None of them stops it.

3. **The ramp is on project time.** Speed keyframes are absolute project time (js/scene.js:1043-1050, the comment on `speedAdvanceOver`). `FM.layerSourceAdvance` integrates `evalProp(sp, layer.start + i/SR)` from the layer's current start (js/scene.js:966-985). `FM.layerLocalTime` uses that integral (js/scene.js:1089-1101).

4. **Case (i), item starts inside the deleted span.**
   - js/spine-edit.js:407-413 puts the item in `plan.keyless` and lands it at a.
   - The write calls `trimClipEdge(l, 'head', b - s)`, which integrates the ramp over [s, b] correctly, but it sets only `duration` and `trimStart`.
   - `applyPlan` then sets `l.start = a` and skips `shiftKeys` because the item is keyless (js/spine-edit.js:668).
   - Result: the footage that used to play from b now plays from a, but the ramp is read at a+x instead of b+x, so it lands (b-a) late against the footage.
   - Removing the keyless flag would not fix it either: d = a - s, but the needed shift is a - b.

5. **Case (iii), item runs through the span.**
   - js/spine-edit.js:425-436: `FM.splitLayer` gives B the speed keys from a onward (splitAnimated, js/app.js).
   - B is head-trimmed by len with `B.start` left at a, and B is in neither moves nor lands, so its keys never move.
   - Same (b-a) offset.

6. **Worked example.** Song at 5..11 with a linear ramp 0.5x at 5 to 2x at 11. Delete B = [4, 8), the next clip starts at 8.
   - After the cut, at project time 4.5 the source sits at about 2.875 s.
   - The frame that used to be there (old project time 8.5) was at about 3.281 s.
   - That is 0.41 s of drift, and it keeps growing, so sync is lost and the end of the source shifts.

7. **The design does not intend this.** DESIGN.md §3.6's Delete row says a cut unit's keys go through `riderKeys(u, f)` (release 2.4). Until then 2.1 refuses cut items with keys. The ramp is an absolute-time key list like the others, so leaving it out of the count creates exactly the half-applied edit that 2.1's refuse-rule exists to prevent.

8. **Full is not affected.** `planDelete` is Simple only.

Severity: minor is fair. It needs a ramped long video or sound that is not yet pinned and overlaps the deleted clip.

title: Phone: More stops working once its sheet has been closed
scenario: At 380, select a clip, tap More, and the sheet rises. Close it with the grab bar or a swipe down. Simple never sets m-editing (app.js:1010), so mobile.js:180-181 call dismiss(), which latches userClosed=true (mobile.js:37) and keeps the selection; panelFor is still that clip. Tap More again: openPanel sets panelFor and calls refreshAll, and syncSheet runs. The selection key has not changed, so userClosed stays true and it returns at mobile.js:92 without raising the sheet. More now does nothing until he picks another clip and comes back.
why: In 2.2, More is the only way to every setting the tray does not have (speed, volume, effects, and so on), and the phone is his main device. Nothing explains why it went dead.
fix: Make openPanel force the sheet up: expose a small FM.mobile hook that clears userClosed and opens it. Or have the Simple-mode dismiss call FM.simpleTools.closePanel(), and clear userClosed whenever panelFor is set again.

verdict.evidence:
The defect is real. I followed the whole path in .claude/worktrees/980-phase2 and none of it stops the scenario.

1. **Simple never sets m-editing.** `app.js` (syncSelectionChrome) does `document.body.classList.toggle('m-editing', !simple && phone && n === 1 && !selOwns)`.
   - So `styles.css:4207` (`body.m-editing #insp-grab { display: none; }`) never applies in Simple, and the grab bar is visible at 380.
   - Nothing keyed on `ed-simple` or `sm-` hides `#insp-grab`.

2. **Closing latches `userClosed`.** The grab bar's click (`mobile.js:178`) calls `dismiss()`. The swipe callback (`mobile.js:179`) is `if (isPhone() && body has m-editing) FM.selectLayer(null); else dismiss();`, so in Simple it also calls `dismiss()`. `dismiss()` at `mobile.js:37` sets `userClosed = true; close();`. The selection is kept.

3. **Nothing clears `panelFor` or `userClosed` on close.** `closePanel` has no caller anywhere in `js/` (grep finds only its definition). No observer watches the sheet closing. `userClosed` is reset only when the selection key changes (`mobile.js:56`) or when nothing is selected (`mobile.js:57`).

4. **Tapping More again does nothing.** The tray's More runs `FM.simpleTools.openPanel(id)` (`simple-tools.js:125`, 234): `panelFor = id; lastSig = ''; FM.refreshAll()`.
   - `refreshAll` (`app.js` ~940) calls `FM.inspector.refresh()`, which is mobile.js's wrapped version (`mobile.js:184-187`), so `syncSheet()` runs.
   - The key is the same id, so `userClosed` stays true.
   - `sheetHeld(id)` is false because `panelFor === id` (`simple-tools.js:239`). `selectMode` is off and `_sheetSuppressFor` is null.
   - `mobile.js:92` (`if (userClosed) return;`) returns, so `open()` is never reached.

5. **The other ways in are hidden.** `#insp-toggle` is `display: none` at every width, so it gives no other way to open the sheet. The only recovery is to change the selection key: pick another clip, or deselect and reselect, which also clears `panelFor` in `sync()` at `simple-tools.js:213`.

6. **No test covers it.** The only More test (`tests.js` ~121497, smTrayCheck at 380) taps More once and never closes and reopens the sheet. Nothing in the plan (BUILD-PLAN-PHASE2.md:4177, "More raises today's panel") says a closed sheet should leave More dead.

The workaround is slightly wider than the claim says (deselect and reselect the same clip also brings it back), but More on its own is dead until the selection key changes.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Smallest fix that leaves Full untouched: tapping More clears the sheet's dismissed latch. Full never calls `openPanel` (only Simple's tray does), so Full does not change.

js/mobile.js:456, add one hook to the exported object (`userClosed` is in init's scope):
```js
FM.mobile = { open: open, close: close, toggle: toggle, isPhone: isPhone, openAdd: openAdd, closeAdd: closeAdd, syncAddSheetTop: syncAddSheetTop,
  unlatch: function () { userClosed = false; } };   // Simple's More: a deliberate request for the panel undoes a past swipe-away
```
js/simple-tools.js:234:
```js
openPanel(id) { panelFor = id; lastSig = ''; if (FM.mobile && FM.mobile.unlatch) FM.mobile.unlatch(); FM.refreshAll(); },
```
`refreshAll` then calls `syncSheet`. The key is the same and `userClosed` is now false, `sheetHeld(id)` is false, so `open()` and `dockSheet()` run.

An alternative, if closing the sheet should also end the panel: in `mobile.js`, `dismiss()` would call a new `FM.simpleTools.dismissPanel()` first, which would return false unless `isSimple() && panelFor`. If it returns true, `dismiss` only calls `close()` and does not latch. It needs the `isSimple()` guard, because `panelFor` survives a switch from Simple to Full (`sync()` returns before clearing it when not Simple). Without the guard, Full's dismiss would go through `refreshAll` and raise the sheet straight back up. The hook above is smaller and safer.

Catching test: in `tests/tests.js` smTrayCheck, inside the `width <= 700` branch, straight after the "the panel covers the tray" check:
```js
document.getElementById('insp-grab').click(); await v.sleep(200);
document.getAnimations().forEach(a => { try { a.finish(); } catch (e) {} });
if (insp.classList.contains('open')) throw new Error('380 px: the grab bar did not close the panel');
smTool('more').click(); await v.sleep(200);
document.getAnimations().forEach(a => { try { a.finish(); } catch (e) {} });
if (!insp.classList.contains('open')) throw new Error('380 px: More did nothing after the panel was closed with the grab bar');
```
On the current code the last line fails: `mobile.js:92` returns on `userClosed`. With the fix it passes. The Full control that follows in the test is unaffected.

title: Length field: a typed value can't be committed on an iPhone, and focusing it zooms the page
scenario: On his iPhone, tap Length, then tap the value field. Its font is 14px (styles.css:11801-11802) and the viewport has no maximum-scale (index.html:24), so iOS Safari zooms the page in. The repo already documents this at styles.css:5030 and :7448. inputMode='decimal' brings up the iOS decimal pad, which has no Return key. The only commit is a keydown Enter (simple-tools.js:169), and the keyboard bar's Done just blurs. There is no change or blur handler, so the value he typed is thrown away and the clip keeps its length.
why: Typing an exact length is one of 2.2's Length features, and on his phone it is unusable. The zoom also pans the screen off the bar.
fix: Use font-size 16px on .sm-len-v. Commit on the 'change' event (it fires on blur) as well as on Enter. Set enterkeyhint='done'.

verdict.evidence:
I tried to refute this and could not. Every part of the claim matches the code in /Users/ezrasmith/Claude/FreeMotion/.claude/worktrees/980-phase2.

1. The field can only commit on Enter. In js/simple-tools.js:167-169 the input is built with `val.inputMode = 'decimal'`. Its only listener is `keydown`, and it returns unless `e.key === 'Enter'`. The file has no `change`, `blur` or `focusout` listener for it (I grepped simple-tools.js and simple-timeline.js). The row's own Done button (lenBack, :163) sets `lengthFor = null` and re-syncs without reading `val`, and −1/+1 (:165) also ignore it. So once the field loses focus, the typed value is dropped and the clip keeps its length. The field also goes on showing the typed number until the next re-render, which is misleading.

2. The iOS decimal pad (inputmode=decimal) has no Return key, so on his iPhone that Enter never arrives. Android's number pad does send Enter, so Android and desktop work. The one test of this (tests/tests.js:121568, and the plan at BUILD-PLAN-PHASE2.md:3757-3758) fires a synthetic `KeyboardEvent('keydown', {key:'Enter'})`, the one event the iPhone pad cannot produce. That is why the suite misses it. The plan's "exact code" has the same Enter-only design, so the build follows the plan, but the plan's bug is real. DESIGN.md:2713 asks for "a typed value" that commits a ripple trim and gives no Enter-only exception.

3. The zoom is real. styles.css:11801-11802 sets `.sm-len-v` to `font: 700 14px/1`. No later rule overrides it: I checked the `hover:none` and `pointer:coarse` blocks and found no global input font rule. index.html:24 has `width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, viewport-fit=cover` with no maximum-scale, and no JS changes the viewport. The repo itself warns that iOS zooms the page into any field under 16px (styles.css:5030 on #hm-search-input, and :7448-7449 on .set-aikey-input, from the queue 930 review). This field breaks that rule.

4. The proposed fix needs one correction. A naive "commit on change as well as Enter" commits twice when Enter is pressed: keydown commits, then `val.blur()` fires `change` synchronously, while `S.edit` is async (js/spine-edit.js:789), so the duration has not changed yet. A typed value equal to the current length would also hit `planTrimTail`'s `|dt|<1e-9 -> refusePlan('nothingMore')` (spine-edit.js:~471) and show a false "nothing more" line. The commit needs a guard. Also, `enterkeyhint` does not add a Return key to the iOS decimal pad. It only helps Android. The real fix for iPhone is committing on `change`.
