title: PC: the line's button lands where 🗑 was, so a second click deletes a locked clip
scenario: At 1280, select a locked main clip and click 🗑 (sticky at band x 253-307). refuse('locked') runs inside the click and puts 'That clip is locked [Do it anyway]' in the row. .sm-say-t (flex:1) pushes the button to the right edge, about x 201-295, which covers 🗑's old spot. The 56px keep-clear exists only under max-width:700 (styles.css:11774, 11812). The line never times out while the mouse rests on it (the :hover check at simple-timeline.js:90). So a 'did that work?' re-click 400ms or more later presses Do it anyway, which unlocks and deletes the clip.
why: DESIGN §3.12 rule 5: while a line shows, the right 56px of the row has no button, and buttons are left-aligned after the text, 'so a quick double tap on 🗑 can no longer land on Do it anyway'. The 400ms arming only stops fast double clicks.
fix: Apply the .sm-line padding-right:56px at every width, or left-align the buttons after the text as DESIGN says.

verdict.evidence:
I tried to refute this and couldn't. Every link in the scenario holds in the 980-phase2 worktree:

1. On PC the tray and the line share one row. index.html:613 puts #sm-tray and .sm-line together inside #sm-say. simple-tools.js:52-57 (place()) appends #sm-bar to #inspector-panel whenever the (max-width:700px) query fails, so on PC it sits at the bottom of the band. DESIGN §3.12 1(b) agrees: "On PC it takes the tray's place in the band."

2. 🗑 is pinned at the right edge on PC too. In simple-tools.js trayFor, the delete tool has pin:true and goes last in every kind's list. styles.css `.sm-tool.sm-pin { position: sticky; right: 0; margin-left: auto; padding-left: 16px }` has no media query. With global border-box (styles.css:106), min-width 54 and the "Delete" label, 🗑 covers about [W-54, W]. In Studio at 1280, --insp-w is 307, so 🗑 spans x 253-307, which matches the claim.

3. Clicking 🗑 on a locked main clip refuses synchronously with a Do it anyway button. The click runs S.cmd.del, which calls S.edit (spine-edit.js:867). planDelete adds the clip to removes and touched (:392). lockedOf finds it, and :810 calls refuse('locked', {retry: ... unlock:true}). That calls S.say with buttons [doAnyway] (:734, :760), all before the first await. Deleting an unlocked clip with a locked clip after it ends up in the same place.

4. The line pushes its button to the right edge on PC. When .sm-saying is set, #sm-tray is hidden and .sm-line is shown (styles.css ~11788-11790). .sm-line has `padding: 0 12px`, and `.sm-say-t { flex: 1 1 auto }` makes the text fill the row, so the single button ends at W-12. "Do it anyway" (700 12px plus 24px padding) is about 94-100px wide, giving roughly [W-106, W-12]. That covers about 42 of 🗑's 54px, including its centre. The only keep-clear rules are phone-only: `@media (max-width:700px)` at styles.css:11774, then 11812 (`#sm-say.sm-say-has-b .sm-line { padding-right: 56px }`). Nothing at min-width:701 adds one.

5. Nothing stops a slower second click. With a mouse, ptrDown is false by the time click fires, because the capture-phase pointerup at simple-timeline.js:72 runs first. So in sayLine (:116-117) `up` is true, and armed() becomes true 400ms after t0. The document pointerdown clear (:71) skips targets inside sayEl. The button's click handler (:122) calls clearSay() and then bd.fn(), which is the retry with unlock:true, and the locked clip is deleted. armClear (:87-93) keeps re-arming every 1s while the pointer hovers over sayEl, so the line stays under a resting mouse.

6. The contract is not phone-scoped. DESIGN.md:1465-1467 (rule 5) says that while a line shows, "the rightmost 56 px of the row (🗑's slot) holds no button and takes no tap ... no button may overlap the rectangle 🗑 had in the tray it replaced. So a quick double tap on 🗑 can no longer land on Do it anyway". Rule 1(b) puts the row in the band on PC. BUILD-PLAN-PHASE2.md:1860/3643 kept the phone-only media query from 2.1, when PC's #sm-say sat under the timeline with no 🗑 in it. Release 2.2 moved the tray, and 🗑 with it, into #sm-say on PC, so that scoping became a defect. The 400ms arming only stops double clicks faster than 400ms; the existing test (tests.js:121131) checks only that timing, never the geometry.

Mitigations, none of which refute it: ↶ can undo the delete. The fix touches only #sm-say, which only Simple builds, so Full does not change.

title: Stay put on a multi-selection makes one undo step per item and quietly stops after five
scenario: Select 8 lyric text lines (in Full, or with shift-click on PC), switch to Simple, and tap the tray's Stay put. ids.forEach calls S.cmd.stay once per id, and each call is its own S.edit. The first sets S.running and awaits applyPlan. The next four go into the queue (spine-edit.js:792, `S.queue.length < 4`). The 6th to 8th get 'One moment — still finishing the last edit.' and are dropped. Result: 5 of 8 lines stay put, the history has 5 steps, and the say line gives no hint that 3 lines were skipped.
why: DESIGN §8.5b says a multi-selection's Stay put is one commit, and §3.2 rule 6 says refuse rather than half-apply. Lyrics, eight back-to-back lines, are the DESIGN's own example.
fix: Use one S.edit whose plan sets the stay flag on every selected id (a planStayMany), so it is one commit and one undo step.

verdict.evidence:
I traced the path end to end and could not refute it. It is slightly worse than claimed.

1. js/simple-tools.js:224-227. With 2+ ids that are all non-main, the tray's Stay put runs `ids.forEach(id => S.cmd.stay(id, true))`. That is one S.edit per id. tool() at :79 calls t.run(b) directly, with no await and no guard. BUILD-PLAN-PHASE2.md:2770 has this same forEach, so the plan itself carries the bug.

2. js/spine-edit.js:1271. `stay(id,on)` is `S.edit(label, R => S.planStay(R,id,on))`, and planStay (:1139-1146) is a flag-only plan.

3. js/spine-edit.js:789-799. Call 1 sets `S.running = true` synchronously and runs until `await applyPlan(plan)` (:818). applyPlan is async (:654), so even with an empty `plan.pre` it yields, and control returns to forEach while S.running is still true.
   - Calls 2-5 hit :791-792 and are queued while `S.queue.length < 4`.
   - Calls 6-8 hit the else branch: `S.say(line('wait'))` ('One moment — still finishing the last edit.', spine-words.js:50), then return false. They are dropped with nothing retained.

4. Each run calls `FM.history.commit` (:836). history.commit (js/history.js:289-312) has no coalescing; it only drops a snapshot identical to the last. Each edit flips a different layer's sm.stay, so the result is 5 undo steps, and in a session 5 collab transactions. That breaks §3.7's "one edit = one undo step = one collab transaction" (spine-edit.js:766) and DESIGN §3.2 rule 6, "Refuse, never half-apply" (DESIGN.md:593).

5. Even the 'wait' line does not survive. Call 1 finishes in a microtask after the dropped calls have spoken, and speakDone (:850-854) then says the live 'Stays put' line. The drain (:779-788) re-runs calls 2-5, and each says 'Stays put' again. So the screen ends on "Stays put" and gives no hint that 3 lines were skipped.

6. Extra symptom: after the first edit, :831 collapses the multi-selection to `[sel0]`. The user sees "8 selected" turn into one item even though up to 7 lines were never processed.

7. Reachability is confirmed. DESIGN §8.5b (DESIGN.md:2809) brings a 2+ selection into Simple from Full, shift/⌘-click or ⌘A. FM.selectionIds (app.js:3531) returns scene.selectedIds, and nothing in editor-mode.js clears it on a switch. Text lines are non-main, so `all` is true and the button shows.

I found no guard, coalescing or batching that saves it.

title: Phone: tapping the tray's empty space or a line's text deselects and dismisses the line
scenario: At 380, select the song. The tray shows Stay put, More and 🗑, with 🗑 pushed right by margin-left:auto, leaving about 160px of empty #sm-tray. Tap that space. The document deselect-on-empty-tap handler's KEEP list has #timeline and #inspector-panel but not #sm-timeline or #sm-bar, which sit in #timeline-panel on the phone. So it calls FM.selectLayer(null), and simpleTools.sync then clears panelFor, lengthFor and the line. The same happens for a tap on a line's text, which DESIGN §3.12 rule 2 says 'does nothing', and for a tap in the 56px keep-clear. A quick double tap on 🗑 of a locked clip puts the second tap on .sm-line's padding: the clip is deselected and 'That clip is locked' is gone before he can read it, although rule 5 says that space 'takes no tap'. Tapping the selected clip itself also goes through this deselect first, so it closes an open Length row or More panel on both phone and PC.
why: His selection and the line he was reading disappear on a near-miss in the toolbar, and the row's own stated guards are defeated.
fix: Add '#sm-timeline, #sm-bar, .sm-menu' to KEEP. They are display:none in Full, so Full is unchanged, and simple-timeline.js:58-62 already handles a tap on empty timeline space.

verdict.evidence:
I couldn't refute it. I traced every step in the worktree (HEAD f368458d), reading the code only; nothing was run.

1. **The handler.** The deselect handler is a document capture listener (js/app.js:9220-9302). It decides `keepAtDown` at pointerdown by `e.target.closest(KEEP)` (app.js:9270). KEEP (app.js:9220-9237) lists `#preview, #timeline, #transport, #inspector-panel, … button, input, …`. It does not list `#sm-timeline`, `#sm-bar`, `#sm-say`, `#sm-tray` or `.sm-menu`, and the 2.1/2.2 diff of app.js leaves KEEP untouched. The `'button'` entry matches the tag only, so `div[role=button]` does not count. At pointerup, if the tap did not move, no overlay owns the screen and something is selected, it calls `FM.selectLayer(null)` (app.js:9298-9303). Nothing stops it first: a stopPropagation on the same node cannot, and the only stopImmediatePropagation in js/simple-tools.js is on #btn-opts' click.

2. **Where the rows sit.**
   - `#sm-timeline` is a sibling of `#timeline` inside `#timeline-panel` (index.html:593-602), not inside it.
   - On a phone, `place()` puts `#sm-bar` inside `#sm-timeline` (simple-tools.js:52-54). Only on PC does it go into `#inspector-panel` (:55), which is in KEEP. So the tray and line problems are phone only.

3. **Empty tray space.** The tray is `display:flex` (styles.css:11790) and 🗑 is pushed right with `margin-left:auto` (:11798). A song gets `[stay, more, del]` (simple-tools.js:147), so there is a large stretch of bare `#sm-tray`. A tap there means target is the `#sm-tray` div, so `keepAtDown` is false and the selection is cleared.

4. **What clearing does.** `selectLayer(null)` runs `syncSelectionChrome()` synchronously (app.js:3558), which calls `FM.simpleTools.sync()` (app.js:1012). That clears `panelFor` and `lengthFor` (simple-tools.js:213-214), and the change in `selKey` calls `clearSay()` (:212). So the line he was reading goes too.

5. **The line's text and keep-clear.** The `wireSay` pointerdown spares taps inside `#sm-say` (simple-timeline.js:72), but the app.js handler does not. So a tap on `.sm-say-t` or on `.sm-line`'s 56px right padding (styles.css:11812) still deselects and dismisses whenever something is selected. That breaks DESIGN §3.12 rule 2 ("A tap on the line's own text does nothing and does not dismiss it") and rule 5 ("takes no tap"). It also breaks T19 Round 3 ("tapped twice 80 ms apart … stays and stays locked with its line shown").

6. **Locked clip, double tap on 🗑.** The refusal comes through `refuse('locked', …retry)` (spine-edit.js:734, 810) with a Do it anyway button. That sets `sm-say-has-b` and hides the tray (:11789). The second tap at 🗑's old spot lands on `.sm-line`'s padding, so the clip is deselected and the line is cleared at once.

7. **Tapping the selected clip (phone and PC).** `.sm-item` is a `div[role=button]` (simple-timeline.js:166-175) and `#sm-timeline` is outside KEEP on both layouts. So the document pointerup clears the selection before the item's click re-selects it, and `panelFor`/`lengthFor` are already gone, which closes More or Length. It may be worse: `selectLayer(null)` → `timeline.rebuild()` → `simpleTimeline.rebuild()` (timeline.js:5683-5687) rebuilds the item, removing the tapped node during pointerup. I believe Chromium drops the click when the pressed node is removed, which would leave nothing selected. I'm not certain of that browser behaviour, but the fix removes the risk either way.

8. **The suite doesn't catch it.** The existing 2.1/2.2 tests use `.click()` or keys, which never send pointerdown/pointerup.

9. **Full stays the same.** `#sm-timeline` and `#sm-bar` are `display:none` outside `body.ed-simple` (styles.css:11682, 11784), and `.sm-menu` only exists in Simple. Simple's own empty-timeline deselect is still handled by `#sm-inner`'s click handler (simple-timeline.js:58-62).

**Side issue (not this claim):** `body.sm-running #sm-timeline` is `pointer-events:none` (styles.css:11779). While a command runs, a tap there falls through to `#timeline-panel` and still deselects; this fix does not cover that.
verdict.corrected_fix:
The suggested fix is right as given. In js/app.js:9225, append to the KEEP string:

  ' #topbar, #topbar-m, .sb-handle, #sm-timeline, #sm-bar, .sm-menu, button, input, select, textarea, label, a, option, [contenteditable],' +

What each entry covers:
- `#sm-timeline` covers the phone's tray, line and keep-clear, since `#sm-bar` lives inside it on a phone. It also stops a tap on the selected clip from deselecting before the item's own click.
- `#sm-bar` covers the tray on PC.
- `.sm-menu` covers taps on the padding of the Sound / ⋯ menu, which sits on body.

Simple's empty-timeline deselect is still handled by `#sm-inner`'s click (simple-timeline.js:58-62). Full is unchanged because all three are `display:none` or absent outside `body.ed-simple`.

Test that fails before the fix and passes after: 'simple P2.2 · at 380 a tap on the tray's empty space, on a line's text or in its 56 px keep-clear, or on the selected clip keeps the selection, the line and an open More / Length'. Use the tap helper described below, not `.click()`.

1. In Simple at 380, select the song so the tray is Stay put · More · 🗑. Take the midpoint between More's right edge and 🗑's left edge. As a precondition control, `elementFromPoint` there must return `#sm-tray`. Tap there and assert `FM.scene.selectedId` is still the song.
2. Select a main clip. Call `FM.spine.say('That clip is locked', { buttons: [{ label: 'Do it anyway', fn(){} }] })`. Tap on `.sm-say-t`, then tap 20px from the right edge of `.sm-line`, which is in the keep-clear. After each tap, assert the line text is still there and the clip is still selected.
3. `FM.simpleTools.openPanel(id)`, then tap the selected `.sm-item` (pointer events, then `.click()` on the re-queried item). Assert `FM.simpleTools.panelFor() === id`. Repeat with `openLength(id)` and assert the tray still has the `.sm-len-v` input.
4. Positive controls: the same tap plus a click on empty `#sm-main` still clears the selection. In Full, the same synthetic tap on the empty stage still clears it.

**The tap helper:** dispatch `new PointerEvent('pointerdown' / 'pointerup', { bubbles: true, clientX, clientY, button: 0, pointerType: 'touch' })` on the element at that point. The handler is a document capture listener, so it sees these synthetic events.

Mutation proof: removing `#sm-timeline` from KEEP turns cases 1–3 red.

title: Keys pressed in the tray, the project tools or Simple's menus run Full's global shortcuts
scenario: At 1280, with a main clip selected, open Simple's ⋯. Focus goes to 'Close all gaps' (role=menu). Press ↓, as a menu invites: app.js:9061 nudges the selected clip's picture 1px down and commits on keyup, a hidden canvas write in Simple. Escape falls through to inspector.back() (app.js:9170), which deselects and leaves the menu open. Tab is always prevented and selects the next layer (app.js:9115), so the tray (role=toolbar) and Clips, Text, Sound and Overlay can never be reached from the keyboard. Space on a clicked tray tool toggles play (9059) instead of pressing it. Backspace with focus on a tool deletes the main clip through onKey.
why: DESIGN §8.10 4a (FM.simpleKeyScope: native Tab, arrows, Space and Enter left to the focused control, Escape closing the menu) is not written anywhere. The new role=toolbar and role=menu controls invite exactly these keys.
fix: Write simpleKeyScope for focus inside #sm-bar or .sm-menu, called right after the inEdit check, and handle Escape, arrows and Home/End inside openMenu (closeMenu, with focus going back to its anchor).

verdict.evidence:
The claim is real for Simple's popup menu (Simple's ⋯ and the Sound tool's list). It is overstated for the tray and the Space key, and I'd call it minor/moderate, not major. I reasoned from the code only and ran nothing.

What I confirmed in the worktree:
- **The menu takes focus but owns no keys.** `js/simple-tools.js:182-192` `openMenu` builds a `role=menu` of `role=menuitem` buttons and focuses the first one (line 191). It has no keydown handler. It closes only on an item click (185), an outside pointerdown (70), or leaving Simple (`sync`, 205). It matches the plan's text exactly (`BUILD-PLAN-PHASE2.md:2725-2735`), so this is a gap in the plan that the build copied, not a slip from the plan.
- **Nothing in app.js stops keys aimed at the menu.**
  - `app.js:8952`: `inEdit` covers only INPUT/SELECT/TEXTAREA/contentEditable, so a BUTTON target counts as "not editing".
  - `app.js:8970`: `overlayOwnsScreen()` checks for a fixed element covering 90% of the screen. `.sm-menu` is about 210 px wide (`styles.css:11805`), so this is false.
  - `editor-mode.js:241-283`: `onKey` returns false for ArrowDown and for Escape. For Backspace/Delete with one main clip selected it runs `S.cmd.del`.
- **↓ in the menu edits the clip.** The arrow branch (`app.js:9061-9091`) writes `transform.y` +1 on the selected unlocked clip. The keyup handler (`app.js:9196-9198`) then commits an undo step.
- **Esc reaches through the menu.** It falls to `app.js:9145-9171`, then `inspector.back()` (`inspector.js:7014-7027`), which calls `FM.selectLayer(null)`. Nothing closes `.sm-menu`. This is the same bug queue 690 fixed for the right-click menu (see the comment at `app.js:9146-9156`).
- **The app already has the right pattern.** Its existing `role=menu` (`contextmenu.js:68-84`) handles Escape, ↑/↓ and Home/End itself and calls stopPropagation. The new menu does not.

Result: with a main clip selected at 1280, open Simple's ⋯ and press ↓. The clip's picture moves 1 px and that becomes an undo step. Backspace deletes the selected main clip. Esc deselects the clip and leaves the menu open.

What I refuted or would downgrade:
1. **Space after clicking a tool.** DESIGN §8.10 4a itself says Space still means play after a mouse click. So Space toggling play there is the design, not a defect.
2. **Tab never moving focus.** That is Full's existing app-wide handler (`app.js:9115`), and it was already true before this diff. §8.10 4a (the key-scope rules) is part of Phase 1 by DESIGN's "Phase 1 unless noted". `BUILD-PLAN.md:2497` pushed "Simple's own key scope" to "a Phase 2 row". But no release in `BUILD-PLAN-PHASE2`'s table (lines 64-69, 2.1 to 2.6) schedules it. That is a gap in the plan to log, not something 2.1/2.2 were supposed to build.
3. **Keys on a clicked tray button.** Backspace and arrows there do exactly what they do with focus on the page body: the designed Simple Delete, and the arrow nudge that has existed since Phase 1. So the tray adds no separate harm.
4. **"Focus goes to Close all gaps."** That only happens when there is a gap or overlap (line 197). Otherwise focus lands on "Loop and preview speed…".

The claim's suggested fix, a full `FM.simpleKeyScope` in `app.js`, is bigger than needed and touches the handler Full shares. A fix local to the menu solves the real part and leaves Full untouched.

title: A tray tool loses focus after any press that changes the clip
scenario: With keyboard focus or VoiceOver on Move later, press Enter. The move changes l.start and R.main, so the signature at :216 differs and tray.textContent='' (:219) removes the focused button. Focus falls to <body> and a second Enter does nothing. The same happens with +1 frame and −1 frame, Stay put and Duplicate. Refusal lines with buttons hide the whole tray (display:none) and never move focus to their first button.
why: DESIGN §3.12 1(a): 'The pressed tool stays mounted and keeps focus, so Move earlier can be pressed three times in a row by thumb or by Enter'. §8.10 item 6 makes this the screen-reader route for arranging clips. The comment at simple-timeline.js:94-95 says the same.
fix: Before rebuilding, note the focused element's data-tool (and whether the Length input had focus), then focus the matching new node afterwards. For lines with buttons, focus the first button and give focus back to the tool when the line goes.

verdict.evidence:
I tried to disprove this and could not. The path runs like this.

1. Pressing Move later calls tool()'s click handler (js/simple-tools.js:79), then t.run, then S.cmd.move (js/spine-edit.js:1268), then S.edit. That calls FM.refreshAll() (js/spine-edit.js:835), which runs simpleTimeline.rebuild, which calls FM.simpleTools.sync() (js/simple-timeline.js:311; also js/app.js:1012 from syncSelectionChrome).

2. In sync(), the signature at js/simple-tools.js:216 includes l.start, l.duration and JSON.stringify(l.sm), plus the R.main id order and seam kinds.
   - A move changes both l.start and the main order.
   - +1/−1 frame changes l.duration.
   - Stay put changes l.sm.
   - Duplicate changes R.main, and the selection may change too.
   So `sig !== lastSig`, and :219 runs `tray.textContent = ''`. That removes every child, including the focused button. tool() (js/simple-tools.js:71-81) always makes new button nodes.

3. Nothing gives focus back. grep for focus/activeElement in simple-tools.js, simple-timeline.js and spine-edit.js finds only openMenu's focus (simple-tools.js:191) and armClear's hover/focus check (simple-timeline.js:90). There is no data-tool lookup anywhere in js/. Focus drops to <body>, so a second Enter does nothing.

4. Other tray buttons lose focus the same way. lenEdge (Start/End) and lenBack set lastSig='' and rebuild (simple-tools.js:163-164).

5. The success line does not cause this. speakDone sends a button-less result to {live:true} (spine-edit.js:862), which goes to #sm-live only (simple-timeline.js:109). So the tray stays visible, and the rebuild alone takes the focus.

6. The refusal half of the claim is also real.
   - sayLine (simple-timeline.js:107-129) adds sm-saying. styles.css:11789 then sets `#sm-say.sm-saying #sm-tray { display: none; }`, which hides the focused tool.
   - sayLine never focuses its first .sm-say-b, and clearSay (simple-timeline.js:86) never gives focus back.

7. The contract asks for exactly what is missing:
   - DESIGN.md:1437 (§3.12 1a): the pressed tool "stays mounted and keeps focus".
   - DESIGN.md:1450-1451 (1b): when a line with buttons appears, "focus moves to its first button", and when it dismisses, focus returns to the tool that raised it (or the tray's first tool).
   - DESIGN.md:2969-2970 (§8.10 item 6): "focus stays on the pressed button".
   - DESIGN.md:2711 says the same.
   The code's own comment at simple-timeline.js:94-95 claims this too.

8. No test in tests/tests.js checks that tray focus is kept, which is why the suite stayed green.

This bug affects only Simple. Full never builds #sm-tray.

title: In Simple, ⋯ can't close the Loop / preview speed bar it opened
scenario: Simple ⋯ → 'Loop and preview speed…' opens Full's #opt-bar and lights ⋯ (.active). Pressing the lit ⋯ again, which is how Full closes it, is caught by the capture listener and opens Simple's menu. The only way to close the bar is ⋯ → 'Loop and preview speed…' a second time.
why: The obvious way to close the bar never works in Simple.
fix: In the capture listener, let the click through to Full's handler when #opt-bar is open.

verdict.evidence:
I tried to refute this and couldn't. Every path I followed confirms it.

1. The intercept. js/simple-tools.js:67 adds a capture-phase click listener on #btn-opts. It checks only `!isSimple() || FM._smOptsPass`, then calls `e.stopImmediatePropagation(); e.preventDefault(); optsMenu(opts)`. It never looks at whether #opt-bar is already open.

2. Opening the bar. The menu item at js/simple-tools.js:198 sets `FM._smOptsPass = true`, calls `o.click()` synchronously, then clears the flag. The capture listener lets that one click through to Full's bubble handler at js/app.js:7478-7481: `const open = !FM.sideBarOpen(optBar); FM.setSideBar(optBar, optBtn, open)`. That handler is a toggle. setSideBar (app.js:7346-7353) removes `.hidden` and adds `.active` to #btn-opts, so ⋯ shows as lit.

3. The second tap. The next real tap on the lit ⋯ comes with isSimple() true and _smOptsPass false. The capture listener swallows it and opens Simple's menu, so Full's toggle never runs and the bar stays open. The document pointerdown listener at simple-tools.js:68 only closes Simple's own `.sm-menu`, not the bar.

4. No other way to close it. `FM.closeOptBar` (app.js:7474-7475) is defined but has no callers anywhere in js/. Nothing else calls `FM.setSideBar(optBar, …)`. I found no outside-tap or Escape close for #opt-bar, and the mode switch (editor-mode.js:123-153, apply) doesn't close it either. Nothing in Simple's CSS hides #opt-bar or #btn-opts (styles.css:11686-11701). In Simple, the only way to close the bar is ⋯ → "Loop and preview speed…" a second time. That re-runs the toggle, but the label gives no hint that it closes anything.

5. The plan doesn't make this intended. BUILD-PLAN-PHASE2.md:4178 says the menu's other item "passes through to Full's own ⋯ strip". It says nothing about how to close it. The only Simple ⋯ test (tests.js:121619-121635) never opens the strip from Simple, so nothing covers this.

Full is unaffected either way, because the listener returns at once when not in Simple. Severity minor is right: the bar can be closed, just not the obvious way.

title: Every line that takes the row is announced twice by a screen reader
scenario: Delete a clip that has a title. sayLine writes the text and its Undo button into .sm-line inside #sm-say (role=status, aria-live=polite), then writes the same text into #sm-live (a second polite status, :127). VoiceOver or NVDA reads 'Deleted clip and 1 thing on it, Undo' and then 'Deleted clip and 1 thing on it'.
why: Every refusal and every line with Undo is read twice.
fix: Write #sm-live only for live lines, or announce row lines through one of the two regions only.

verdict.evidence:
I tried to disprove it and couldn't. The double announcement comes straight from the markup and the one function that writes lines.

Markup (index.html:613, 616):
- `#sm-say` is `role="status" aria-live="polite"`. It holds `#sm-tray` (`aria-live="off"`) and `.sm-line`. The `.sm-line` has no aria-live of its own, so it takes polite from `#sm-say`.
- `#sm-live` is a second `role="status" aria-live="polite"` region (class `sm-vh`: visually hidden but still in the accessibility tree).

How a row line is written, `sayLine` in js/simple-timeline.js:107-128:
- The `opts.live` branch (:109) writes only `#sm-live` and returns. That case is fine.
- Every other line goes the row route. It empties `.sm-line` (:112), adds the class `sm-saying`, which flips `.sm-line` from `display:none` to `flex` (styles.css:11787-11788), then appends the text span (:113) and up to two `<button>`s (:119-123). These are additions inside a polite region, so the region reads the text plus the button labels.
- Then :127 runs unconditionally: `if (liveEl) liveEl.textContent = text;` That updates a second polite region with the same text in the same task.

The claim's scenario follows this exact path:
- `S.cmd.del` leads to `speakDone` (js/spine-edit.js:858-863). For a delete that took items with it, `plan.say` is set, so it calls `S.say(text, { buttons: [Undo] })`.
- `S.say` passes this to the sink, `FM.spine._setSink(sayLine)` (js/spine.js:95-99, simple-timeline.js:347).
- The result is the row route with no `live` flag, so both regions fire.
- Every refusal (spine-edit.js:760), the 'wait' and 'skipped' lines (:773, :784, :793), Clips' "Add clips" chooser (simple-tools.js) and the song line (simple-timeline.js:322) take the same route.

Ways I tried to refute it, none of which hold:
1. Is either region hidden while the line shows? No.
   - On a phone, `#sm-bar` and `#sm-live` are both inside the visible `#sm-timeline`.
   - On a PC, `place()` (simple-tools.js:50-56) moves `#sm-bar` into `#inspector-panel`, the visible left band. Tests at tests.js:120226 and :121501 assert that `#sm-say` is a 52 px row on screen.
2. Would a screen reader de-duplicate? No: the two strings differ. `#sm-say` adds the button labels ("… Undo"), so identical-text suppression could not fire. Polite updates queue.
3. Does the plan ask for the double? Not for anything in this diff. DESIGN.md §3.12 rule 1(b) makes `#sm-say` itself the `role=status` polite region for button lines. Rule 1(a) sends button-less lines to `#sm-live` only. The one case the design says is "written to `#sm-live` as well" is a remote ripple's "Sam moved 4 clips" (§10.4). That line is not built in Phase 2: the only `live:true` caller is spine-edit.js:862.
4. Does anything depend on `#sm-live` holding row text? No test reads `#sm-live` (grep of tests/ finds nothing). No code reads `liveEl.textContent`.

Caveat: this is not new in Phase 2. Base 5888368e already had `#sm-say role=status aria-live=polite` (index.html:609-610 there) and the same unconditional `if (liveEl) liveEl.textContent = text;` (simple-timeline.js:100 there), for the Phase 1 refusal plus "Open in Full" line. Phase 2 keeps the defect and widens it: every refusal, every line with Undo, the "Add clips" chooser and the song line now go through it.

Whether it is heard twice depends on the screen reader. NVDA and JAWS on Chrome read both queued polite updates. VoiceOver usually does too, but can drop one. Hence 0.8 and not 1.0.

title: Three tools' accessible names don't contain their visible labels (WCAG 2.5.3)
scenario: aria-label is set from title: 'Into row' is named 'Put in the clip row' (:152), '−1 frame' is 'One frame shorter' and '+1 frame' is 'One frame longer' (:165). Voice Control 'tap Into row' or 'tap plus 1 frame' finds no matching control.
why: Voice and switch users can't reach these tools by the words on screen.
fix: Set aria-label to the visible label and keep the longer wording in title.

verdict.evidence:
I tried to disprove this and couldn't. The scenario happens as the reviewer describes.

- js/simple-tools.js:76 (`tool()`) runs `b.title = t.title || t.label; b.setAttribute('aria-label', t.title || t.label);`. So whenever a tool has a `title`, that title replaces the visible label as the accessible name. The `<svg>` is `aria-hidden` (:42), so the visible text the button shows is only `<span class="sm-tool-l">` (:75).
- The words in js/spine-words.js:99 and :101 are:
  - `into: 'Into row'` / `intoTitle: 'Put in the clip row'`
  - `minusFrame: '−1 frame'` / `shorter: 'One frame shorter'`
  - `plusFrame: '+1 frame'` / `longer: 'One frame longer'`
- These are passed as `title` at simple-tools.js:152 (Into row, overlay tray) and :165 (the Length row's − and + steps).
- In each of the three pairs, the name does not contain the visible text. That fails WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name (Level A).
- The two other titled tools pass by luck. 'Lift off the clip row (make it an overlay)' contains 'Lift off', and 'More settings for this' contains 'More'.
- The labels really are visible. styles.css:11792-11795 lays `.sm-tool` out as icon over text with `.sm-tool-l { white-space: nowrap }`, and nothing hides it, including in `#sm-tray.sm-tray-len` (:11800). So 2.5.3 applies.
- No test pins these names. Searching tests/tests.js for 'Put in the clip row', 'One frame shorter', 'One frame longer' and 'intoTitle' finds nothing.
- Full is untouched: this is Simple-only DOM.

Mitigating point: the contract itself asks for this. DESIGN.md:2915 says **Put in the clip row** is the full name for `title, aria-label, drag labels`, and BUILD-PLAN-PHASE2.md:2619 copies the same line of code. So the build follows the plan, and the plan is what breaks 2.5.3.

The impact is real but minor. Voice Control users saying 'tap Into row' or 'tap plus one frame' match no control, and those users fall under DESIGN §8.10 item 6 ('Every drag has a button route… so a screen-reader or switch user can arrange clips'). The Length −/+ buttons are that button route for trimming.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Smallest fix, in js/simple-tools.js:76:
```js
b.title = t.title || t.label; b.setAttribute('aria-label', t.label);
```
The accessible name becomes the face word. The longer title stays in `title`, and since `title` is no longer used for the name, browsers expose it as the accessible description, so screen readers still hear "Put in the clip row" / "One frame shorter". No new strings are needed, so T20 (all words in spine-words.js) still holds.

Alternative if the contract's full name must be part of the name itself: `b.setAttribute('aria-label', t.title && t.title.toLowerCase().indexOf(t.label.toLowerCase()) < 0 ? t.label + ', ' + t.title : (t.title || t.label));`. This keeps the visible label at the start of the name.

Also amend DESIGN.md:2915 (§8.9 words table) to say the full names go in `title` (the description) and that `aria-label` starts with the face label.

Test (fails before, passes after). Name it `980 2.2 tray names contain their visible labels (WCAG 2.5.3)`, run in Simple at 380 px:
1. Select a main clip and collect `#sm-tray .sm-tool`.
2. Select an overlay and collect again (this includes Into row).
3. Call `FM.simpleTools.openLength(mainId)` and collect the Length row (−1 frame, +1 frame, End, Done).
4. Also collect `#sm-tools .sm-tool`.
5. For every button, assert that `(b.getAttribute('aria-label') || '').toLowerCase()` contains `b.querySelector('.sm-tool-l').textContent.trim().toLowerCase()`, and throw naming `data-tool` when it does not.

Positive control: Lift off and More pass both before and after. Before the fix, 'into', 'lenMinus' and 'lenPlus' fail ('put in the clip row' does not contain 'into row'; 'one frame shorter' does not contain '−1 frame').

title: The quiet line can show '0:60'
scenario: summary() rounds the seconds after splitting off the minutes (m = floor(secs/60), s = round(secs − 60m)). Two 29.8s clips (59.6s) show '2 clips · 0:60', and 119.5s shows '1:60'. Phase 2's quiet line (simple-tools.js:175) is the first place this is shown.
why: A wrong time in the row he sees whenever nothing is selected.
fix: Round the total first: t = Math.round(secs); m = Math.floor(t / 60); s = t % 60.

verdict.evidence:
I tried to refute this and couldn't. The bug is real and easy to hit.

1. The formula, at js/spine-words.js:120-122:
   `const m = Math.floor(secs / 60), s = Math.round(secs - m * 60);`
   followed by `m + ':' + (s < 10 ? '0' : '') + s`.
   The minutes are floored before the seconds are rounded. Any remainder in [59.5, 60) therefore rounds up to s = 60 and m is never carried:
   - secs = 59.6 gives m = 0, s = 60, so "0:60"
   - secs = 119.5 gives m = 1, s = 60, so "1:60"
   Nothing clamps or carries the value.

2. The input is a raw float. At js/simple-tools.js:175, quietLine calls `FM.spineWords.summary(clips.length, R.trackEnd || 0)`. R.trackEnd is set at js/spine.js:357 as `clipsOnly[clipsOnly.length - 1].end`, which is start + duration in seconds, unrounded. Ordinary footage reaches the bad range: two 29.8 s clips, or a 59.7 s video. The Length tool (simple-tools.js:167) also changes duration by sign/fps per tap. Repeated additions of 1/30 leave values like 59.99999999, which also print "0:60".

3. He sees it in normal use. simple-tools.js:222 runs `if (!ids.length) { tray.appendChild(quietLine(R)); return; }`, so the line shows whenever nothing is selected.

4. This is the first place it appears. `git grep` at base 5888368e finds no caller of spineWords.summary; only the definition exists, at line 66. tests/tests.js has no assertion on summary output, so nothing would catch it.

Only the severity can be argued: it is display-only and corrupts no data. "minor" is accurate.
